chapters.title: Chapter 1951 Second of the three gifts
paragraphs: "Then link with it."
The Seer spoke, and just as Nux glanced at her with a doubtful look on his face, she smiled and nodded.
"Yes, Eternity won't know. Don't worry."
Nux smiled.
"But where did you find a weapon of this level that is not connected to Eternity? I thought all Relics were connected to them."
He couldn't help but frown.
"You wouldn't under—"
"Now you are just doing it on purpose, aren't you?"
Nux called her out and at his reaction,
"Hahaha~"
The Seer laughed out.
"Tsk."

Nux snorted, already knowing that the woman would not answer him. He was frustrated, yes, but seeing the woman laugh like that, he just sighed in defeat and focused on linking with the weapon she had brought.
"So how do I do it? Just like you link with normal Relics?"
Nux questioned.
"That is correct."
The woman nodded.
Nux nodded back as he held the Bloodedge and pointed the blade right in the middle of his forehead. Then his forehead and the point of the sword touched.
Bzzz
The Bloodedge trembled, and a drop of blood rolled down Nux's forehead, down to his nose.
Bzzz
A part of his blood was absorbed by the Bloodedge. The crimson veins pulsed brighter than ever, as if she was enjoying drinking blood.
Nux felt that strange, creepy energy he had sensed earlier entering his body, hiding itself from any sort of detection. Then, finally, his flaring sword calmed down.
He could feel it—the connection was made.
And to prove that,
Nux could feel the Bloodedge had started sucking his energy.
"She needs this much energy when she isn't even being used?"
He questioned, somewhat surprised. This much energy drain could pretty much cripple a normal Complete Sovereign within three seconds. Again, this was when the sword wasn't being used.
"Well, she was what they called a failed weapon."
The Seer chuckled.
"What...?"
"She is strong, yes.
She can be used by any being at any level, yes.
But the energy she needs is simply too high for it to be worth it."
Nux frowned at those words.
"But wouldn't the problem be solved as you go to higher levels and have more energy reserves?"
After all, that was how Relics worked, and this was the reason Sovereigns or Primordials weren't given one.
Most of the time, they weren't strong enough to wield one.
However, as one gets stronger, wielding a Relic only brought an advantage.
The Seer, however, shook her head.
"As I said, she can be used by any being at any level. Even an Ascendant or a Protector could wield it. Just that... they would never be able to use it."
"Of course, the Energy Drain would kill them before they would be able to do anything."
"Exactly."
The Seer nodded.
"The Sovereigns, Primordials, Transcendents, and even the Infinities face the same problem."
Nux blinked. Soon, however, he realized what the woman was talking about.
"While a Sovereign wouldn't last for long, a Primordial would be able to wield her for an hour. However, this is only when they merely wield her.
To use her, one would need to feed her more energy, and the energy required to kill a Primordial using her is twice the energy a normal Primordial would have."
"And the same is true for..."
"Higher levels too. To kill a Transcendent using her, one would need as much energy as a normal Transcendent would have.
For an Eternal, she needs half the energy an Eternal would have.
And for Infinity, she needs a tenth of an Infinity's energy.

So the number of times she can be swung by a wielder is extremely limited. A Sovereign and Primordial can never swing her. A Transcendent can swing her once, an Eternal twice, and an Infinity ten times.
And of course, this is just for when you swing her. If your hit misses or the opponent dodges, all the energy is wasted."
"What in the hell..."
Nux blinked in surprise as he stared at the sword in his hand, which seemed to be feeding on his energy without a care in the world.
"She's pretty much unusable. How is she even a Supreme Level Relic?"
"She is above a Supreme Level Relic."
The Seer answered.
"She is an Absolute Relic."
"Yes, you have not heard of that term."
The Seer nodded.
"Absolute Relics are Relics that are stronger than Supreme Relics, but they are so strong that they cannot be wielded."
The woman then looked at the sword in Nux's hand and,
"She is one of them.
One cannot wield her, but if, by chance, there appears a being who can, she is the strongest weapon that being could hope for.

She is the strongest there is. No other Relic can be compared to her. It doesn't matter what sort of Defensive Relic your enemy has—if you attack him using her and the attack connects, she will cut him down."
The Seer spoke with absolute certainty.
"Even if it is a Supreme Level Relic, if given enough energy, she can cut it down."
Nux raised his eyes, overwhelmed. Once again, he stared at the sword in his hand and couldn't help but be impressed.

"She is so strong that when she was created, it was said that if one day, she finds a wielder, she will be the strongest weapon there is, and her wielder will become the most dangerous man in the entire Universe."
The Seer once again glanced at Nux and smiled playfully.
"And now I give her to you.
Do you have the courage to wield her?"
"Heh."
Nux grinned.
"The all-knowing Seer should know the answer to that question already, shouldn't she?"
The Seer grinned at those words as well.
"Why else do you think I gave her to you?"
"Thank you."
Nux smiled as he expressed his gratitude. He gently touched Bloodedge's blade and,
"She is the best gift someone has ever given to me."
The Seer, however, smiled at those words.
"That will change very soon.
After all,
She is only the second of the three gifts I have prepared for you."

chapters.title: Chapter 1952 Are you saying... that my father is becoming what Shadow is to Nux...?
paragraphs: "She is the best gift someone has ever given to me."
The Seer, however, smiled at those words.
"That will change very soon.
After all,
She is only the second of the three gifts I have prepared for you."
Nux blinked for a moment.
Then, he stared at the woman in front of him and,
"You do know that I do not consider my wives as my gifts, correct?
So if you plan on presenting yourself to me as a gift, it won't count."
For the first time since she appeared, the Seer's mouth twitched.
She knew the shameless bastard would say such a thing. She knew it...
Yet...
It was still annoying.
In the end, she just held herself back and,
"My third gift is not me. You would need to put in a lot of work for that, Nux Leander.
I am not a gift. I am a trophy."
"Heh, if the feminists heard you say that..."
Nux chuckled at his own joke as he shook his head.
The Seer just shook her head.
"Take care of her."
The Seer spoke as she pointed at Bloodedge.
"I will."
Nux nodded.
"I hope we meet soon, Nux."
"You can come—"
Before Nux could complete his words, the woman disappeared from his vision. He sensed the space around him and couldn't detect her, even when he expanded his senses to their limit.
A frown appeared on his face before he finally realized it.
'She slowed me down and went away so I wouldn't be able to trace her...
Her powers are just absurd.'
He shook his head, sensing goosebumps all over his body.
"Nux? What is that sword?"
Then suddenly, he heard a question.
He turned around and saw Aeliana and the others looking at him with frowns on their faces.
"That bitch was here, wasn't she?"
Amaya quickly connected the dots.
"The Seer..."
Aeliana's face turned grim.
"That woman was here?"
Faustina blinked her eyes.
"When?"
"We wouldn't know."
Aeliana answered.
"She slowed the time around us, conversed with him, and returned. For us, barely a millisecond would have passed."
"Huh? What sort of power is that...?"
The Progenitors blinked in horror.
"Welcome to the Universe."
Allura chuckled playfully.
"And what is that sword?"
Vyriana questioned.
"A Relic."
Nux answered.
"A Relic?"
Vyriana raised her eyebrow, trying to reach for Bloodedge. Nux, however, shook his head.
"You wouldn't be able to wield her."
And of course, Amaya raised her eyebrows at those words.
"Come on, she is just a sword."
"So why is she a she?"
"I told you before, didn't I? Relics have consciousness. She is the same."
"Yes, but why is her consciousness a she?"
Amaya questioned, appearing right in front of Nux as she leaned forward, staring at Bloodedge.
Of course, everyone here was used to her antics. What surprised them the most was that...
Aeliana was doing the same.
The poor sword was being stared at by two crazy women who seemed like they were ready to destroy her.
Nux very quickly stored her back into his storage ring as he then gained everyone's attention.
"Alright, that's enough playing around. It is time we get serious."
"What did... the Seer say?"
Aeliana questioned. Her tone showed her hesitation.
After all, just like Nux, she had mixed feelings regarding the woman.
"She said that she did all this on purpose. She knew Lord Azriel would survive. She told me that he was bound to become the Universe's Child. She just hastened that process."
"You seem to believe her now."
Amaya narrowed her eyes.
"My instincts warn me whenever I am around her, but maybe I am misreading it..."
Nux then narrowed his eyes as his mind started thinking,
"...maybe they aren't warning me but are trying to tell me something instead."
Amaya and Aeliana stared at him in silence.
Then suddenly,
"Hmm? Was that woman here?"
Everyone heard a voice as a being materialized next to them.
"Father."
Aeliana smiled as she hugged her father. Azriel smiled as he hugged her back.
His eyes, however, were on Nux.
"Yes, she was."
Nux nodded.
"So I was right."
"Hmm? What do you mean?"
"I felt the flow of time around me tremble, so I guessed it would be her."
"You felt the flow of time tremble...?"
Nux raised his eyebrow.

"Ah, yes. Perks of being connected to the Universe. I can see everything with my own and through the Universe's eyes. So I can sense the flow of time, the fabric of space, energies of life and death, and all that stuff."
Others stared at the man with ridiculous looks on their faces. Nux and Shadow, however, were different.
"Shadow?"
Nux muttered out loud as a shadow then materialized in front of him and nodded.
"It is similar to how I perceive your universe."
Azriel raised his eyebrow as he glanced at Shadow.
The woman shrugged. Unlike the others, for some reason, she wasn't intimidated by his gaze.
"I can sense the fabric of space inside Nux's universe, though I cannot sense the flow of time. But maybe that is because it does not exist in there."
Azriel narrowed his eyes at those words.
"Are you saying... that my father is becoming what Shadow is to Nux...?"
"The Universe's Wife?"
Nux chuckled.
Azriel's mouth twitched at those words.
"Stop thinking about it."
Nux then waved his hand.
"It is pointless to try and explain things we do not understand."
"You seem much more easygoing after your meeting with her."
"I am only following your words, Father-in-law."
"If only you were this obedient."
"I listen, okay."
"Right."
Nux turned silent, and not wanting to talk to this annoying man anymore, Azriel just snorted and turned towards the Progenitors.
"Alright, you lot are coming with me."
The Progenitors nodded.
Yes, this was the arrangement made.
The Progenitors would follow Azriel, train under his guidance, and work for him.
While Nux and his wives would do their own thing.
Yes, the race had started.

chapters.title: Chapter 1953 To our Home.
paragraphs: "So what are we going to do now?"
After Azriel took the Progenitors away and only Nux and his wives were left, Astaria turned towards Nux and questioned with a curious look on her face.
Before, their plans were simple: participate in wars, find the worlds to devour, and be connected to Nux.
But now, when they were already connected to him...
Things changed.
"We will do what we were going to do from the very start."
Nux answered her question with a smile on his face.
"Huh?"
Astaria frowned.

Nux's grin then widened as he stared in a certain direction, and with a flick of his finger, he and his wives disappeared, only to appear far, far away, in an open void where everyone's eyes fell on two beings who seemed frozen.
"Wait..."
Astaria's expression changed when she recognized these beings.
One of them was the Leader of the World they had been to in their most recent mission, and the other...
It was a being who had tried to kill them—a Transcendent.
Nux's grin widened, almost turning demonic.
"You didn't think I would forget about them, did you?"
"This... is the Seer's work?"
Astaria questioned, somewhat overwhelmed.
After all, the beings in front of them were a Primordial and a Transcendent! For them to just... float in the void like frozen statues without having any way to retaliate was simply... absurd.
And to think this had continued for weeks.
"It is indeed."
Nux nodded.
"How is... one supposed to defeat someone like her...?"
The Swordswoman questioned.
It was her habit to try and compare herself with everyone who appeared in front of her. At first, she felt like she still had chances.
In the case of Nux, she had already given up, so it didn't matter. Then, Lord Azriel was the same; she knew she couldn't defeat him either.
She believed that it would put an end to it, and as she grew, she would be able to take on most beings in the Universe. But this...
Seeing the Absolute Domination, and all of it being so effortless too...
She wasn't very confident anymore.

Usually, at a time like this, her Master, Vyriana, would have cheered her disciple. After all, she, out of all people, knew that Astaria possessed a potential far higher than most cultivators she had met. But...
This time, even the Dragon was silent.
She couldn't say with absolute certainty that she or her disciple could reach the Seer's level. And it wasn't just her; even Nux, who could sense their thoughts, was silent.
He couldn't lie to his wives.
As much as he loved all of them, the Seer was... someone even he couldn't understand.
He didn't know if his wives could ever surpass her. Heck, he didn't know if even he could ever surpass her.
For now, however, he shook his head.
"You are barely a few thousand years old, Star. You burden your mind too much."
He then teleported Astaria right in front of him as he held her chin, bringing her face dangerously close to his.
"You just focus on cultivating, and I know you will be the strongest.
My wives aren't weak, especially you.
You have proven this time and time again, and you will prove it again."
He reassured his love with absolute certainty.
Astaria looked into his eyes for a moment, and then, unable to resist her body's demands,
She sealed his lips.
'Tsk, I knew she was doing this to get his attention.'
Amaya snorted, and Riona, who saw her daughter's expression, chuckled and gently patted her head.
"What are we going to do with him?"
Aeliana questioned, not liking the attention the Sword Girl was receiving for some reason.

Astaria, who sensed that, stared at the Vampire and narrowed her eyes. Then, as if to spit on her face, she tightened her hug around her husband, shamelessly hoarding him for herself and herself alone.
Aeliana's mouth twitched.
Nux just chuckled as he gently held his Star in his hands, allowing her to hug him as tightly as she wanted.
He, on the other hand, teleported next to the Transcendent, who still couldn't move.
"What are you trying to do?"
Vyriana questioned with a frown on her face, and Nux just grinned.
"Our ally arranged everything so perfectly for us; it would be rude not to take advantage of it, wouldn't it?"
BOOOM
As he said those words, a vast amount of Dark Energy exploded out of his palm, instantly surrounding the Transcendent and the slowed time around him. And before the poor Transcendent could react...
He was devoured.
Yes, Nux devoured him.
With his wives already connected to him and Yrniel safe, nothing else mattered. Even if this man had interacted with his wives before, now, Nux didn't have to hold back.
Their battle would now continue in his choice of battlefield.
"Meh, devour him."
The women, who realized what happened, grinned just like Nux. The group looked no different than a bunch of demons laughing as they played around with the weak.
"What about him?"
Amaya questioned, appearing next to the Primordial.
"Meh, devour him."
Nux shrugged, not paying much heed to the extras.
Could he get his memories and comprehend his Law? Sure.
But was it worth it?
No.
There were trillions of beings in the Universe. If he went around comprehending every single Law he saw, even he would lose his mind.
Amaya nodded as suddenly, dark energy—much more ominous than Nux's—oozed out of her body, instantly swallowing the Primordial.
Ten seconds later, when the devouring mist disappeared, the no-named Primordial was no more.
"Let's return, shall we?"
Nux questioned with a playful smile on his face.
"To our Home."
Felberta smiled gently, and Nux, who stared at his first wife, nodded at her words.
"To our Home."
The demons' shadows then covered their entire bodies, and they disappeared, impossible to be traced by any being in this vast Universe.
Inside Nux's Universe, the Transcendent, who woke up from his slumber as the time around him returned to normal, frowned in confusion, unable to understand where he was.
"Welcome."

Nux's grin then widened as he stared in a certain direction, and with a flick of his finger, he and his wives disappeared, only to appear far, far away, in an open void where everyone's eyes fell on two beings who seemed frozen.
"Wait..."
Astaria's expression changed when she recognized these beings.
One of them was the Leader of the World they had been to in their most recent mission, and the other...
It was a being who had tried to kill them—a Transcendent.
Nux's grin widened, almost turning demonic.
"You didn't think I would forget about them, did you?"
"This... is the Seer's work?"
Astaria questioned, somewhat overwhelmed.
After all, the beings in front of them were a Primordial and a Transcendent!
For them to just... float in the void like frozen statues without having any way to retaliate was simply... absurd.
And to think this had continued for weeks.
"It is indeed."
Nux nodded.
"How is... one supposed to defeat someone like her...?"
The Swordswoman questioned.
It was her habit to try and compare herself with everyone who appeared in front of her.
At first, she felt like she still had chances.
In the case of Nux, she had already given up, so it didn't matter.
Then, Lord Azriel was the same; she knew she couldn't defeat him either.
She believed that it would put an end to it, and as she grew, she would be able to take on most beings in the Universe.
But this...
Seeing the Absolute Domination, and all of it being so effortless too...
She wasn't very confident anymore.
Usually, at a time like this, her Master, Vyriana, would have cheered her disciple.
After all, she, out of all people, knew that Astaria possessed a potential far higher than most cultivators she had met.
But...
This time, even the Dragon was silent.
She couldn't say with absolute certainty that she or her disciple could reach the Seer's level.
And it wasn't just her; even Nux, who could sense their thoughts, was silent.
He couldn't lie to his wives.
As much as he loved all of them, the Seer was... someone even he couldn't understand.
He didn't know if his wives could ever surpass her.
Heck, he didn't know if even he could ever surpass her.
For now, however, he shook his head.
"You are barely a few thousand years old, Star.
You burden your mind too much."
He then teleported Astaria right in front of him as he held her chin, bringing her face dangerously close to his.
"You just focus on cultivating, and I know you will be the strongest.
My wives aren't weak, especially you.
You have proven this time and time again, and you will prove it again."
He reassured his love with absolute certainty.
Astaria looked into his eyes for a moment, and then, unable to resist her body's demands,
She sealed his lips.
'Tsk, I knew she was doing this to get his attention.'
Amaya snorted, and Riona, who saw her daughter's expression, chuckled and gently patted her head.
"What are we going to do with him?"
Aeliana questioned, not liking the attention the Sword Girl was receiving for some reason.
Astaria, who sensed that, stared at the Vampire and narrowed her eyes.
Then, as if to spit on her face, she tightened her hug around her husband, shamelessly hoarding him for herself and herself alone.
Aeliana's mouth twitched.
Nux just chuckled as he gently held his Star in his hands, allowing her to hug him as tightly as she wanted.
He, on the other hand, teleported next to the Transcendent, who still couldn't move.
"What are you trying to do?"
Vyriana questioned with a frown on her face, and Nux just grinned.
"Our ally arranged everything so perfectly for us; it would be rude not to take advantage of it, wouldn't it?"
BOOOM
As he said those words, a vast amount of Dark Energy exploded out of his palm, instantly surrounding the Transcendent and the slowed time around him.
And before the poor Transcendent could react...
He was devoured.
Yes, Nux devoured him.
With his wives already connected to him and Yrniel safe, nothing else mattered.
Even if this man had interacted with his wives before, now, Nux didn't have to hold back.
Their battle would now continue in his choice of battlefield.
"Meh, devour him."
The women, who realized what happened, grinned just like Nux.
The group looked no different than a bunch of demons laughing as they played around with the weak.
"What about him?"
Amaya questioned, appearing next to the Primordial.
"Meh, devour him."
Nux shrugged, not paying much heed to the extras.
Could he get his memories and comprehend his Law?
Sure.
But was it worth it?
No.
There were trillions of beings in the Universe.
If he went around comprehending every single Law he saw, even he would lose his mind.
Amaya nodded as suddenly, dark energy—much more ominous than Nux's—oozed out of her body, instantly swallowing the Primordial.
Ten seconds later, when the devouring mist disappeared, the no-named Primordial was no more.
"Let's return, shall we?"
Nux questioned with a playful smile on his face.
"To our Home."
Felberta smiled gently, and Nux, who stared at his first wife, nodded at her words.
"To our Home."
The demons' shadows then covered their entire bodies, and they disappeared, impossible to be traced by any being in this vast Universe.
Inside Nux's Universe, the Transcendent, who woke up from his slumber as the time around him returned to normal, frowned in confusion, unable to understand where he was.
"Welcome."

chapters.title: Chapter 1954 I was always a fair and just warrior...
paragraphs: The Transcendent, who was now in Nux's Universe, finally returned to his senses as the time flow around him returned to normal.
For him, almost no time had passed.

Just a few minutes ago, he was prepared to complete the mission given to him and appeared in front of those women. However, the instant he appeared in the world those women were supposed to be in, he couldn't find any of them.

He tried asking around, but before he could even react, he was teleported to a different place—a void far away from the world he was in—and very quickly, he recognized the man who teleported him away.
A man who he was supposed to be a threat to, a mere Protector-level being.
Obviously, the information he was given was wrong. He was far stronger than he was told. Of course, it still didn't matter.
No matter how strong he was, he couldn't possibly be at the Transcendent level. With that thought in his mind, he decided to continue the mission and fight.
But then, the space around him started to stretch endlessly, and before he could even think of coming up with a way out, he appeared in this... strange place.
It looked similar to the Void he was in before, but this space seemed... much more ominous... much more... darker.
And much more... incomplete?
He couldn't understand what he felt, but then,
"Welcome."
He heard a familiar voice.
Slowly, he turned around, and a being covered in darkness appeared in front of him.
"It is you..."
He recognized this being. Even though he was covered in darkness, those features were very recognizable.
"You remembered me."
Nux smiled.
"Huh?"
"Ah, my bad. You still think you met me a few seconds ago."
Nux apologized like the gentleman he was.
Then, with the most gentle smile on his face, he started.
"So? Are you prepared to answer my questions?"
"Heh, you dream big."
The being laughed as he disappeared and appeared right next to Nux, prepared to take his hand, but...
"Acckk!!"
The moment he got next to him, Nux simply grabbed him by his neck.
"Oh, you poor thing."
Nux looked at him with a pitiful look on his face.
"You still think you are stronger than me, don't you? I feel like I am bullying you now.
Haaahh...
When did I become a bully?
I was always a fair and just warrior..."
Nux sighed, holding the Transcendent by his neck as if he were a ragdoll.
"Acckk!! Kkkhhh!!"
He couldn't even speak. He had used all his strength, but this monster wasn't even budging!
Protector!?
This monster was a protector!?
Who the fuck was responsible for gathering information related to this mission!?
"Ah, was I holding too tightly?
I apologize.
I am still not used to using my full strength in here, after all."
Nux lightened his grip even further, so much that he ended up releasing the Transcendent instead.
Seeing his chance, the Transcendent quickly rushed away and activated his teleportation artifact, wanting to get away from this monster and abort the mission, but...

Even after using his strongest Spatial Artifact—the one he bought after gathering money for 10,000 years, an artifact that has always protected him and safely brought him back to his base even when an enemy uses anti-teleportation artifacts—he couldn't move.
He...
He couldn't teleport!
His heart skipped a beat. His body tensed up until finally,
Flicker
His body flickered.
'Haahh...'
He sighed in relief.
He thought that the artifact he had spent almost all his life savings on had stopped working, but he was wrong.
'This man must have used a strong anti-teleportation artifact.'
He realized it, but then, he grinned.
'But mine is stronger.'
As he thought about it, his grin widened, and his body disappeared.
...only to appear back in Nux's hand, once again, with Nux holding his neck.
"Ah, I apologize. I am still adjusting to this. You would need to act as a trial thingy."
The Transcendent couldn't believe what was happening.
Why was he back here?
Why wasn't he back in his safehouse?
Does this man have a better spatial artifact than his!?
Was that the reason he was teleported away in the first place!?
He had too many questions. However, he knew the time he had in his hand was limited. Therefore, he decided to use his trump card.
The air changed.
A dark mist oozed from the Transcendent's body. The space around them flickered, almost as if the reality itself was rotting away.
Whoosh
The mist spread fast. Everything around it withered into black dust. The endless void seemed to have turned into what seemed like a void of rot. It looked... sick.
"Heh."
The Transcendent laughed, staring at Nux.
"Welcome to my Domain."
He spoke, regaining his confidence.
Despite being held in such an embarrassing position, he was still grinning. After all, his domain was set. In here...
He was Absolute.
His Law of Rot was the Law of Absolute Rot here.
"I didn't wish to kill you, Nux Leander."
"Oh? You know my name."
Nux raised his eyebrow. He seemed pleasantly surprised.
Which surprised the Transcendent, considering he had the absolute advantage in this battle. However, thinking that the man had lost his mind, he decided to end it.
"Do not blame me. Blame the one who gave me the wrong information."
Saying those words, the Transcendent commanded the Rot to dissolve Nux's entire body. The dark miasma quickly wrapped itself around Nux's body, ready to dissolve his very existence.
But Nux...
"Wrong information, huh...
Now this seems like something I would like to know."
As he thought about it, strange patterns appeared around Nux's body as he started reading the Transcendent's memories.
It was a sight that surprised the Transcendent.
What the hell was he doing?
He was about to die!
His entire body was surrounded by the Power of Rot. His legs should already be dissolved, disappearing from very existence!
Why wasn't he panicking!? Why wasn't he screaming in pain!? Why wasn't the rest of his body weakening!?
Why wa-
"Tsk, this power is creepy. Get rid of it."
Suddenly, Nux commanded, and in an instant, the Transcendent's Domain disappeared, forcefully wiped out by the Universe.
And Nux, of course, was perfectly fine.

chapters.title: Chapter 1955 Any idea who it could be?
paragraphs: "Tsk, this power is creepy, get rid of it."
The instant Nux commanded, the Transcendent's domain disappeared.
The Transcendent widened his eyes in horror, unable to believe what had just happened.
First, it was his Spatial Artifact that malfunctioned, and now even his domain wasn't working properly. What the hell was happening?
He was a high-level mercenary. He had seen his fair share of strange, inexplicable things in this vast Universe, yet this...
This was something he couldn't explain in any way.
The Spatial Artifact was just that—an Artifact. It was normal for it to malfunction, but... even his domain?
This had never happened before.
Something was wrong.
"Confused?"
Nux chuckled.
Already knowing what he was thinking.
The Transcendent stayed silent.

The poor guy had no clue that he wasn't even in his own Universe anymore. He just thought that he was in a different place with no colors, someplace that was slightly different than the Outer Space he knew and didn't think too much about it.
He had seen so many strange places in his life. This one, though different, wasn't enough to surprise him.

Of course, this was only because he didn't understand where he was. If he knew that this not-so-surprising place was an entirely new Universe that he was now part of and that his Law was no longer connected to the Universe he came from but this one,
His reaction would be different.

And once he would learn that the new Universe his Law was now connected to was... this man in front of him—the man he just tried to use it against, the Absolute of this place—his reaction would be even more absurd.
Yes, Nux now held absolute control over his fate. He could even strip him of his hard-earned Law if he wanted, let alone allow him to form or destroy a Domain.
In his own Universe, in front of beings from his own Universe, Cultivation levels didn't matter. Nux's authority here was absolute.
Yes, the moment the being was devoured, his fate was sealed.
"Hmmm, I wonder what I should do with you."
Nux muttered, tightening his hold around the being's neck.
"Aacckk!! Kkkhh!!"
The being struggled, desperately trying to get away, even thrashing his legs, trying to kick Nux, but it was all useless. Nux simply grabbed his leg, which was about to kick him, and tore it off.
"AAAAGGGGHHHHHHH!!!"
The being screeched in pain, but,
"Shut up."
Nux commanded, and he lost his voice.
Finally realizing his situation, the being stared at Nux, wanting to say something in desperation.
Nux allowed him to speak, and,
"I-I did not wish to target you! I didn't do it on purpose! It was a mission! I am not your real enemy, and I have a way for you to meet your real enemie-"
"Yes, Malrik. I know that already."
Nux interrupted.
"H-How do you know my na-"
Malrik's eyes widened in fear, and Nux just grinned.
"I know everything about you, Malrik, the Withering King.
It is quite a grand title you have, a King, huh?"
"T-That is not important. As I said, I took a mi-"

"Yes, you took a mission. The mission was to kill one of my wives and capture the rest, wait for me to appear, and then secretly press the call artifact given to you and summon the ones who hired you.

The way you talk about that would help me meet my real enemies was for me to let you go and allow you to activate your artifact, which would summon those bastards, and in exchange, I will let you go, correct?"
"W-W-What...
How did you..."
Malrik couldn't understand.
Let's forget about the details of the mission and whatnot since those could be leaked. How does this monster know the plan he just came up with?
He didn't even have the chance to share it with anyone!
There was no way to know of this plan unless this man read his mem-
The Withering King realized something, and noticing his changed expression, Nux's grin turned even more demonic.
"You have nothing of value to me, Malrik. There is nothing you know that I do not. So if you wish to be spared, you better come up with something very quickly, or else...
You wouldn't like what is going to happen to you."
Nux spoke as the purest Death Energy gathered on top of his hand.
No, he wasn't going to kill him. He was a Transcendent with a somewhat decent ability, someone Nux could use in the future.
However,
The man had targeted his wives. He couldn't go unpunished either.
So...
"Allegiance! I swear my allegiance to you! I will be your loyal slave and do everything you ask me to! Please! Please spare my life!"
Malrik gave in. Since he couldn't offer anything else of value, he decided to offer himself.
But...
"Hmm? I told you to come up with something different. Why are you suggesting something that is already going to happen?"
"You didn't think you had another choice but to serve me, did you?
Malrik Dannas, you will swear your allegiance to me, whether you want it or not. But for now...
It is time you see my vindictive side."
As he said those words, Nux used Death Energy to push Malrik's soul out of his body. Then, he created his own clone that was given a few needles, while he himself disappeared.
He didn't have the time to torture him on his own. He needed to deal with bigger matters.
Nux reappeared in front of his wives with a solemn look on his face.
"We were wrong when we thought someone from a Higher Level World wanted to target your mercenary party. He didn't come for you."
He spoke, staring at Ember.
The General nodded with a solemn look on her face. She and the others saw the conversation between Nux and Malrik.
"Whoever gave him that mission knew that I would come to protect you, even if the one who captured you was a Transcendent and the odds were highly stacked against us.
Any idea who it could be?"

Since he even specifically mentioned killing one of you, it must be someone who holds quite a deep grudge.
Any idea who it could be?"
Nux questioned as he stared at his wives.

You didn't attract any attention ever since you left Yrniel,"
Felberta answered with a frown, and as strange as those words sounded, they were indeed correct.
The only attention Nux attracted was the Universe's, and that too, as an anomaly.
Anyone who knew him as an anomaly shouldn't know about his connection with the Leander Family Mercenary Party.
To directly target his wives to get to him...
"It doesn't have to be someone who holds a grudge against you,"
suddenly, Aeliana spoke up.
"Mhm, you said that the mission that Transcendent received was to activate the call artifact and summon them when you appeared.
Whoever the mission lister was, it doesn't seem like he knows exactly how strong you are.
The very fact that he thinks that Malrik could kill your wives before you could get there proves that.
It seems like he feels that even you will be helpless against a Transcendent Stage Being, so why would he want the Transcendent to summon them?"
Amaya jumped in with an explanation as well.
Something that made Nux smile.
"To either capture me alive, making sure I do not self-explode trying to protect my wives or...
To protect me."
Amaya smiled, nodding her head.
"To protect a fake sense of reliance,"
Aeliana muttered.
Then, the Vampire looked into Nux's eyes.
"Now, who is it that does not know the full extent of your power, doesn't care about your wives' lives, and wants you to rely on him?"
And very quickly, the list narrowed down to one being.
"My dear father,"
Nux's face turned cold.
"I was expecting him to return. He came later than I expected,"
Astaria commented.
"How convenient, isn't it?"
suddenly, Aeliana chuckled.
"He returned when my father was asleep."
She pointed out.
After all, all of this did happen after Azriel went to sleep. Everything about him becoming the Universe's child happened after this.
"He was waiting for his chance, huh..."
Vyriana raised her eyebrow, impressed.
"So what do we do now?"
Felberta questioned, staring at the rest of the women, and silence fell over the place.
"There is an option of doing what Malrik suggested and summoning the ones who gave the mission. It might lead us to Zylarith,"
Allura suggested.
"But what after that?
What are we going to do even after we reach Zylarith?"
Eisheth questioned.
Amaya nodded at those words.
"We know practically nothing about that man. All we know is that he is in his Soul Form and hiding from the Universe. He cannot use his powers, sure,
but he found the means to list a mission and pay a price generous enough for a Transcendent Stage Mercenary to accept it."
"I agree, the price to hire a Transcendent isn't cheap,"
Ember nodded.
"Most of those are the Heads of Mercenary Halls, earning a lot more than what many believe. For a mission to make them move, the price would be quite big."
"It was a High-Level Relic,"
Nux answered.
He had seen the details of the mission through Malrik's memory.
"A High-Level Relic, huh..."
Ember muttered.
"So that father of yours has something like that..."
Eisheth muttered, staring at Nux.
Nux laughed.
"He must have a lot more than that.
He was the Progenitor of a once Supreme World, after all."
"But still, he wouldn't be able to do all this alone. He still needs to hide his presence. He must have people working for him."
"Of course, how hard do you think that is for a being like him?
He manipulated the Umbrasol Progenitors into doing what he wanted. What is stopping him from manipulating another High-Level World?"
Nux pointed out.
"Are you saying that he has a High-Level World working under him?"
Thyra questioned.
"I am just considering it to be the worst-case scenario. He cannot play his games with a Supreme-Level World; those beings would erase his existence before he could do anything."
"There are chances that they might be working together."
"If they were, a Transcendent wouldn't be the one sent after me. There would have been no need for plans or anything like that. They would have captured you all together with me."
Nux answered, and Aeliana nodded.
"That is correct. The last thing he wants right now is to attract the Supreme Worlds' attention. It has to be a High-Level World or a weaker one."
"It is a High-Level World,"
Amaya spoke with confidence.
"A Middle-Level World handing out a High-Level Artifact would be too suspicious."
Nux nodded at those words.
"So... our enemy is a High-Level World?"
"Yes,"
Amaya and Aeliana nodded with certainty.
"And... what are we supposed to do about it...?"
Vyriana questioned.
A High-Level World meant an encounter with an Eternal, and defeating an Eternal...
"It is impossible,"
Nux, who knew what his wives were thinking, muttered with a solemn look on his face.
"It would be different if I could devour them and bring them into my Universe where I am Absolute and can do whatever I want,

but for that, I would need them in a still position for a few seconds, similar to how it happened with Malrik. With our strength, let alone having them still, even getting close to an Eternal is next to impossible."
Silence fell over the place.
The women continued to think of a way around, but nothing came to their minds. Defeating Eternals was impossible, so what were they supposed to do?
"What if you break through and become a Transcendent?
Can you defeat an Eternal then?"
"I can, but..."
"Then let's leave this matter aside and shift our focus on gathering all the Primordial Energies,"
Amaya declared, and though unwilling, the rest of the women nodded, agreeing with those words.
"Well...
We will, but,"
Nux suddenly spoke up.
"Let's at least try and find out what my father is planning, no?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1957 Submit to my Lord
paragraphs: Bzzz Bzzz Bzzz
"Huh?"
A 1-meter-tall being with a silver body, a goblin-like appearance, and a hunched back frowned as suddenly, his storage necklace trembled.
With a simple tap, the necklace shone, and suddenly, a small red marble appeared in his hand, vibrating nonstop.
The moment he realized what it was, his expression turned solemn.
Then suddenly,
Flicker
Another being, 4 meters tall with a thin green body, similar to that of a mantis, with two long legs and hands that ended with blades, appeared in front of him.
A similar marble was in his arms, and he stared at the silver goblin with his yellow eyes.
"What do we do?"
The Mantis-like being questioned, his voice indicating the urgency of the matter.
The Silver Goblin, however, remained silent, something the mantis didn't like.
"Nixgut! We do not have time!"
He shouted, and Nixgut, the Goblin, stared at him and narrowed his purple eyes.
"He hasn't reported for weeks, and now, after all this time, he tries to call us to a dimension he had never reported before. This stinks of a trap."
"We went to that world he was in before. They told us he suddenly disappeared together with their Leader."
The Mantis-like being muttered, even he was doubtful.
"He was clearly captured, and now the enemy is trying to find his accomplices. If the enemy is actively calling us, then it must mean he is prepared to face us."
Nixgut spoke with certainty.
"The enemy was told to be a Protector."
The Mantis-like being retorted.
"Zharak, do you not see it?
What Protector is capable of teleporting a Transcendent? That being clearly has a helper. If we go there, it will be no different than running to our own death."
"Well..."
Zharak, the Mantis-like being, lowered his head.
"If we go, we might die—a probable death.
But if we don't..."
Zharak stared at his artifact, which was still ringing, and said,
"Then they will not let us go—a certain death."
Nixgut turned silent.
"Don't forget, they have the artifact as well. They must know that the artifact was activated. If we do not go, it would mean that we abandoned the mission and...
Abandoning their mission in the middle is nothing different than a death sentence. I wouldn't be surprised if they are already aler-"
Before Zharak could even complete his words,
Bzzz Bzzz
Another artifact buzzed, and the instant they realized which one it was, the two stared at each other, fear evident in their eyes.
Slowly, they activated the artifact, and a voice Nixgut would recognize was heard.
[Why hasn't the Call Artifact stopped buzzing yet?]
It was a simple question, yet both Zharak and Nixgut gulped.
"W-We were about to leave. It is j-just that it was a-activated later than we expected. The d-dimensions were different tha-"
Nixgut tried to reason, but...
[Are you planning on abandoning the mission?]
"No, NO! Of course not!"
Zharak raised his voice, desperately showing that he had no desire to do such a thing.
"I-It is just that t-this might be a trap they have carefully s-se-"
[If it is a trap, go and fall into it. The two of you are Transcendents. If you are afraid of a Protector, then you might as well lose your life in that trap.]
The voice countered.
Then, in a tone much heavier than before, it continued,
[Activate the Call Artifact if you think you are not strong enough. I will send reinforcements.
Now move.
And if you return without that boy, do not bother returning.
Try and run away. I would like to see how far your capabilities reach.]
The artifact then stopped shining.
The line was cut.
Zharak and Nixgut stared at each other, both cursing the time when they took the mission. In the end, they just sighed as they prepared to teleport to the dimension they were summoned to.
Both of them took out their Spatial Artifact and,
Flicker Flicker
They disappeared.
"You are here."
As they reappeared in a world they had never been to, they heard a voice.
It was Marlik.
"So it was you."
Zharak narrowed his eyes.
He seemed to know who Marlik was. After all, there were only a handful of Transcendent Stage Mercenaries, and the three of them were quite popular.
Yes, before they met, Zharak and Nixgut didn't know the Mercenary they were in contact with was Marlik.

They had simply given out a mission that required a Transcendent. It didn't matter which Transcendent took it, and usually, to prevent any information leak, it is generally preferred that whenever a mission has to be divided into two missions, unless necessary, the two parties shouldn't know about each other.
Not that it was much of a big deal. The one who hired them wasn't the kind to care about such matters, but they still kept it professional and hid their identities from each other.
"Why did you call us here? Did you fail the mission?"
Nixgut questioned, seeming more worried about the mission.
At the same time, he also noticed that Marlik was oddly silent. For a blabbermouth who would never shut up, this was strange.
Just as he expected, something was wrong.
"Marlik, what is happening?"
Nixgut questioned as he narrowed his eyes.
Zharak was the same. He sensed the strangeness in Marlik's behavior as well.
"My Lord wishes to talk to you."
Marlik finally spoke up. His voice was the same as before, but his tone was much different than before.
"Your Lord...?"
As people who knew Marlik for a long time, both Nixgut and Zharak found this strange.
Marlik was extremely arrogant.
He called himself a King, after all!

Even if he called someone a Lord, he had never once shown this much respect to anyone before. Even when they did missions together with him, and it required them to show respect to the ones who gave them missions, he was never... this subdued.
Right now, he seemed no different than a loyal subordinate who would even give his life away for his master.
Something that Marlik could never do.
If the two of them hadn't sensed that vile energy oozing out of him, they would have never believed he was the same man they knew.
"Submit to my Lord, and you will live."

chapters.title: Chapter 1958 The one you stand against cannot be defeated.
paragraphs: "Submit to my Lord, and you will live."
Marlik spoke, his tone the same as before, filled with respect when he talked about his lord.
Both Zharak and Nixgut frowned in confusion.
He was asking them to submit?
This was...
"Where is the Boy, Marlik?"
Zharak questioned directly, having had enough of this sick game.
"My Lord is not here."
"Your Lord? That Boy is your Lord?"
"It would do you well if you show him respect. I will not sit and let you disrespect my Lord."
"And what are you going to do? Use that filthy power of yours? On me?"
Zharak laughed.
He was confident in his skills. After all, despite both of them being Transcendents, he was far stronger than Marlik.
Marlik, however, didn't seem bothered by Zharak's remark. Rather, he just stared at Nixgut.

"I can see that the two of you took the Mission from someone else. For there to be two different Missions to deal with this matter, and considering the reward I was promised was a High-Level Relic, the two of you must have been promised the same, if not more.

Three High-Level Relics—only a Strong High-Level World could give out this reward. So, assuming that the one who hired you was a High-Level World, if you go back empty-handed, I do not have to spell out what your fate will be.
Running away wouldn't be possible either. They must have a way to track you. You two are out of options. It would be wise to submit."
Marlik explained calmly.
"I understand your point."
Nixgut nodded lightly.
"I have a few questions I need answers to regarding this Lord you seem to respect so much."
"Ask."
"How will I be treated if I submit? Will your Lord ensure my safety?"
"If my Lord wishes to protect you, no one in this Universe will be able to harm you."
"Oh? That is quite a bold claim."
"My Lord is that exceptional."
"I can see that."
Nixgut nodded.
"To think he turned you into... this.
Anyways, next question-"
Before Nixgut could even complete his sentence, Zharak, who had disappeared from his side while Nixgut got Marlik's attention, appeared right next to Marlik, ready to cut his limbs.
Nixgut, who saw that, grinned.
Zharak understood what he wanted. This was why he always partnered with him in missions—the two understood each other.
It was a common tactic, really.
With how Marlik talked, it didn't look like that Boy was here, so they decided to deliver Marlik instead. They would question him and extract answers any way they wanted.
Yes, they would need to relinquish the rewards for not being able to complete the mission, but at the very least, they would be able to keep their lives.
That was the plan.
And with Marlik, who would lose his limbs to Zharak's attack, capturing him wouldn't be difficult, especially with his Law.
Nixgut prepared to set his domain, ready to capture him the moment Zharak took him by surprise, but just as Zharak was about to cut Marlik's arm,
Flicker
Marlik disappeared and reappeared right next to Nixgut, placing his hand on top of his head, ready to dissolve his head with his miasma the moment he tried something foolish.
Nixgut, who was caught by surprise, widened his eyes in horror.
This... shouldn't be possible.

Nixgut knew he had a weaker body. Instant attacks like blink could be extremely lethal to him, so he had an artifact that constantly flickered the Space around him, making sure no one was able to teleport next to him.
Marlik... shouldn't have gotten this close to him.
Not to mention... he shouldn't even be fast enough to react to Zharak's attacks! Zharak was a lot faster than him!
No, forget all that—the main question was, how did this man teleport in the first place!?
He never had any Spatial abilities, and that artifact he loved so much could only be used if it was loaded with dimensions beforehand.
"This is why I suggested you submit."
Suddenly, Nixgut heard a voice.
"You are going against a force you do not yet understand."
"W-What...?"
Nixgut muttered, his voice still laced with fear. After all, his life was in this man's hands. The moment he sensed even the simplest movement, Marlik would kill him, and he knew it.
"Watch."
Marlik then turned Nixgut's head to Zharak, who stood still as well, not wanting Nixgut to get hurt because of his movement.
Then suddenly,
Flicker
Zharak disappeared.
"W-Wha-"
Before Nixgut could understand what happened, Marlik forcefully raised his head, forcing him to look up, to where Zharak was teleported to.
And then,
Flicker Flicker Flicker Flicker

Zharak's body constantly appeared and disappeared at random places. Sometimes, he clashed with trees; sometimes, his body was dragged through the ground; and sometimes, he was just teleported to random places—all this happened in a matter of milliseconds, not even giving him enough time to get back on his feet, let alone resist whatever was happening to him.
Zharak looked no different than a rag doll being experimented on and thrown around by a child who seemed a little too excited.
And Nixgut, who was seeing this happening right in front of him... couldn't believe his eyes.
Zharak was... the strongest of the three of them.
Or at least, that's what it was supposed to be...
But...
To think someone like Zharak would be so helpless...
He wasn't even given enough time to set up his domain.
"W-What is happening...?"
Nixgut questioned.
"This is the being you are trying to go against.
You cannot even sense his presence. You cannot even understand what he is doing. You cannot even sense his Law Flow, and yet...
You still think you can go against him?"
Marlik tilted his head with a light smile, his tone filled with disdain.
"Also, you must have activated your Call Artifact a long ago, did you not?
Do you still not wonder why the reinforcements aren't here yet?
Or do you need more time to realize it?"
"W-What...?"
"This Space is sealed. No one can come here to help you, not even if it is the Progenitor of a High-Level World himself.
No matter how much you wait, there will be no help.
Submit, Nixgut, for the one you stand against cannot be defeated."
A/N: Marlik. Nixgut. Zharak.

Zharak laughed.

After all, despite both of them being Transcendents, he was far stronger than Marlik.
Marlik, however, didn't seem bothered by Zharak's remark.
Rather, he just stared at Nixgut.
"I can see that the two of you took the Mission from someone else.
For there to be two different Missions to deal with this matter, and considering the reward I was promised was a High-Level Relic, the two of you must have been promised the same, if not more.
Three High-Level Relics—only a Strong High-Level World could give out this reward.
So, assuming that the one who hired you was a High-Level World, if you go back empty-handed, I do not have to spell out what your fate will be.
Running away wouldn't be possible either.
They must have a way to track you.
You two are out of options.
It would be wise to submit."
Marlik explained calmly.
"I understand your point."
Nixgut nodded lightly.
"I have a few questions I need answers to regarding this Lord you seem to respect so much."
"Ask."
"How will I be treated if I submit?
Will your Lord ensure my safety?"
"If my Lord wishes to protect you, no one in this Universe will be able to harm you."
"Oh?
That is quite a bold claim."
"My Lord is that exceptional."
"I can see that."
Nixgut nodded.
"To think he turned you into... this.
Anyways, next question-"
Before Nixgut could even complete his sentence, Zharak, who had disappeared from his side while Nixgut got Marlik's attention, appeared right next to Marlik, ready to cut his limbs.
Nixgut, who saw that, grinned.
Zharak understood what he wanted.
This was why he always partnered with him in missions—the two understood each other.
It was a common tactic, really.
With how Marlik talked, it didn't look like that Boy was here, so they decided to deliver Marlik instead.
They would question him and extract answers any way they wanted.
Yes, they would need to relinquish the rewards for not being able to complete the mission, but at the very least, they would be able to keep their lives.
That was the plan.
And with Marlik, who would lose his limbs to Zharak's attack, capturing him wouldn't be difficult, especially with his Law.
Nixgut prepared to set his domain, ready to capture him the moment Zharak took him by surprise, but just as Zharak was about to cut Marlik's arm,
Flicker
Marlik disappeared and reappeared right next to Nixgut, placing his hand on top of his head, ready to dissolve his head with his miasma the moment he tried something foolish.
Nixgut, who was caught by surprise, widened his eyes in horror.
This... shouldn't be possible.
Nixgut knew he had a weaker body.
Instant attacks like blink could be extremely lethal to him, so he had an artifact that constantly flickered the Space around him, making sure no one was able to teleport next to him.
Marlik... shouldn't have gotten this close to him.
Not to mention... he shouldn't even be fast enough to react to Zharak's attacks!
Zharak was a lot faster than him!
No, forget all that—the main question was, how did this man teleport in the first place!?
He never had any Spatial abilities, and that artifact he loved so much could only be used if it was loaded with dimensions beforehand.
"This is why I suggested you submit."
Suddenly, Nixgut heard a voice.
"You are going against a force you do not yet understand."
"W-What...?"
Nixgut muttered, his voice still laced with fear.
After all, his life was in this man's hands.
The moment he sensed even the simplest movement, Marlik would kill him, and he knew it.
"Watch."
Marlik then turned Nixgut's head to Zharak, who stood still as well, not wanting Nixgut to get hurt because of his movement.
Then suddenly,
Flicker
Zharak disappeared.
"W-Wha-"
Before Nixgut could understand what happened, Marlik forcefully raised his head, forcing him to look up, to where Zharak was teleported to.
And then,
Flicker Flicker Flicker Flicker
Zharak's body constantly appeared and disappeared at random places.

Sometimes, he clashed with trees; sometimes, his body was dragged through the ground; and sometimes, he was just teleported to random places—all this happened in a matter of milliseconds, not even giving him enough time to get back on his feet, let alone resist whatever was happening to him.
Zharak looked no different than a rag doll being experimented on and thrown around by a child who seemed a little too excited.
And Nixgut, who was seeing this happening right in front of him... couldn't believe his eyes.
Zharak was... the strongest of the three of them.
Or at least, that's what it was supposed to be...
But...
To think someone like Zharak would be so helpless...
He wasn't even given enough time to set up his domain.
"W-What is happening...?"
Nixgut questioned.
"This is the being you are trying to go against.
You cannot even sense his presence.
You cannot even understand what he is doing.
You cannot even sense his Law Flow, and yet...
You still think you can go against him?"
Marlik tilted his head with a light smile, his tone filled with disdain.
"Also, you must have activated your Call Artifact a long ago, did you not?
Do you still not wonder why the reinforcements aren't here yet?
Or do you need more time to realize it?"
"W-What...?"
"This Space is sealed.
No one can come here to help you, not even if it is the Progenitor of a High-Level World himself.
No matter how much you wait, there will be no help.
Submit, Nixgut, for the one you stand against cannot be defeated."
A/N: Marlik.
Nixgut.
Zharak.

chapters.title: Chapter 1959 Law of Confinement.
paragraphs: "This Space is sealed. No one can come here to help you, not even if it is the Progenitor of a High-Level World himself.

Submit, Nixgut, for the one you stand against cannot be defeated."
Marlik spoke, and silence fell over the place.
Nixgut's thoughts were a mess. He was considering every possible factor, and Zharak, well, he was in no situation to say anything. He was still being teleported around.
There was a time when this torture stopped. However, the moment it did,
"MARLIKK!!!"
Zharak shouted and rushed towards Marlik, trying to end him, and was teleported again.
The only one who could make a sane decision here was Nixgut. Marlik gave him all the time he wanted.
After all, Nux still needed that name.
"W-What if I tell you who posted this mission and all other details? Will you let us go?"
Nixgut questioned, trying to negotiate.
Marlik, however, just chuckled.
"Even if I do, will you be able to survive?
I highly doubt they will let you go after you failed a supposedly impossible-to-fail mission, no?"
Nixgut turned silent. He knew it was the truth.
In the end, he had no other choice but to say,
"I submit."
Marlik's smile widened at those words. Then,
He glanced and made Nixgut look forward and said,
"Form your Domain and capture him."
Nixgut nodded. However, just as he was about to deploy his domain, Marlik tightened his hold over his head and said,
"Do not try and do anything foolish, is that clear? The only reason you two are alive is because you know something my Lord wants to know.
But there are other ways to extract that information, ways that...
Will be very painful."
Marlik warned.
"And don't think holding me hostage would do you any good.
The only way for you to survive is to either submit or return to that High-Level World with my Lord in your hands.
My life has no value in my Lord's eyes. He will never exchange it with his own. He will disregard me in an instant."
The Withering King clarified.
His words made Nixgut raise his nonexistent eyebrows.
'Why does he sound so proud of it?'
He wondered.
'Something's wrong with his head. That Lord of his must have done something.'
For now, however, Nixgut couldn't care less. He did as he was told and deployed his Domain. The moment he did, a strange energy burst out of his body and...
Crack

The very sky shattered like glass, revealing an endless void of black and gold chains twisting through the void. These chains slithered and shifted, creating an overwhelming sense of imprisonment, as if the very world itself was locked in the Prison.

The ground warped into what seemed like an infinite maze of unbreakable obsidian, its surface covered in ancient runes of restriction. The air became dense and unmoving, thick with an incomprehensible force that crushed the target's will to resist.
This was Nixgut's Domain.
A Domain where his Law, the Law of Confinement, turns into the Law of Absolute Confinement.
A Domain where, once Nixgut declares his target, the target would have no way out.
A Domain that automatically locks the Space, making it impossible for the target to teleport or phase into a separate dimension.

A Domain where sound is muffled, and the concept of 'distance' ceases to exist—no matter where the target moves, they remain within the wielder's grasp. Every step they take leaves behind binding runes that tighten around their limbs, draining their strength and preventing them from moving any further.
In this Prison of Eternity, there was no freedom, no loopholes, no hope—only endless captivity.
A Perfect Domain to capture any being. It was the very reason Nixgut was chosen for this mission.
And the moment this Domain was deployed, Nixgut had the absolute Power, the Power he used to capture...
Zharak.
The instant the silver goblin willed it, the chains in the sky moved and wrapped around the Mantis-like warrior. Runes appeared all around his body, making it impossible for him to escape.
"Nixgut!"
Zharak screamed in anger, glaring at Nixgut. His voice, however, didn't travel far. Nixgut could barely hear him.
"You did well."
Marlik praised.
"I hope you keep your word and let me live."
"Of course, my Lord always keeps his word. If there is anything in this Universe you can trust, it is his words."
Marlik praised his lord, putting almost blind faith in him.
Then finally, the Lord appeared in front of them, stepping right into the domain that was capable enough to capture him at any moment.
Yes, even now, if Nixgut wanted, he could have captured Nux. It was just a matter of will, yet...
He didn't do it.
How could he?
Nixgut recognized Nux. He was the same man who, according to what they were told, was merely a Protector-level being, who, even in the worst-case scenario, shouldn't be stronger than a Transcendent.
Transcendent?
This man...?

He looked no different than a mortal who had no cultivation, yet was still walking around in a domain where he could be captured at any moment, and had subdued a Transcendent-level being who used to call himself a King!
Clearly, he wasn't a mortal!
It meant that Nixgut wasn't even strong enough to sense his cultivation level!
And what did it mean...?
This man...
He was far stronger than him. It might even be possible for him to be a High-Level Eternal.
'No wonder this bastard was acting like a loyal little bitch.'
Nixgut finally understood why Marlik was acting so strangely.
Then suddenly, that being glanced at him. His golden eyes seemed full of endless wisdom, and Nixgut didn't miss that aura of absolute confidence around him.
"You think before you move. You seem useful. As promised, I will keep you alive."
The being muttered, praising Nixgut.
"T-Thank you, my L-Lord."
Nixgut nodded.
The being nodded back with a light smile on his face. Then, he glanced at Zharak and said,
"But to do that, I need to hide you from the ones who will be after you. And for that, I will need to take you two to the World I govern."
"A-A World you govern...?"
Nixgut stuttered.
"A-Are you by any chance, talking about your D-D-Domain...?"
He questioned, stuttering without stop.

chapters.title: Chapter 1960 Hello, Father.
paragraphs: "A-A World you govern...?"
Nixgut stuttered.
"A-Are you by any chance, talking about your D-D-Domain...?"
He questioned, stuttering without stop.
A Phase where one finds Unity with their Law and creates a Domain where they have Absolute Control, the power to warp the very reality itself.
A Domain where their Will reigns Supreme—Death, Life, Time, Space, or any concept, they have a say in all.
That was the Eternal Phase.
Yes, if an Eternal wanted, they could hide Nixgut and Zharak in their Domain and make it so no one else in the entire Universe could find them.
This, however, was an extremely limiting option. After all, no matter how strong one's Law was, even if it was an Absolute Law, a Domain was still that—a Domain.
It was limited, extremely limited for that matter.
How could two beings live their entire life in another's Domain?
That was no different than imprisonment.
But...
"Hmm? Why would I talk about my Domain? Do I look like someone who wishes to imprison you? Or does Marlik look imprisoned to you?"
"W-W-What...?"
Nixgut couldn't believe what he was hearing. His eyes had widened in absolute horror. Just considering the possibility that came to his mind gave him chills beyond anything he had ever felt.
"When I say the World I govern, I mean the World I govern. The World I have complete control over. A world you can hide in and live as you please."
The being announced, and Nixgut's entire body trembled.
It was true...
Not a Domain, but...
A World...
That was...
That was beyond the level of the Eternal Phase. That was...
Infinity.
A Level where one's Law becomes a representation of their Self instead. A Level where their Domain turns into a World instead—a World that travels with them, a World they have Absolute Control over.
A World where they were... True Gods.
The Infinity.
The being in front of him...
He was... an Infinity!
No wonder Zharak was being teleported around like some ragdoll. No wonder their teleportation artifacts weren't working. And no wonder the reinforcements weren't here.
No one was able to sense this place because...
This was a World under this being's absolute control. If he didn't want anyone here, there would be no one here.
"I will ask you one last time, Goblin. Do you and your friend wish to swear your allegiance to me?"
The being questioned, and this time, Nixgut smashed his head on the ground and said,
"Yes! Yes, we do! We will swear our allegiance to our Lord and be his most loyal subordinates!"
He submitted, this time, out of his own will.
Who in their right mind wouldn't want to be part of a Supreme World!?

As for questions like why an Infinity-level being from a Supreme World was being chased around by a mere High-Level World, or why a Supreme World was recruiting a mere mercenary, these didn't even appear in Nixgut's head.
He was simply too overwhelmed by everything he saw and heard that he couldn't think straight.
His mind was too occupied by the thought of how glorious his life would be after he got accepted by the Supreme World.
Nux, who knew exactly what he was thinking, grinned. Then,
"Stay still."
He muttered as suddenly, Black Energy oozed out of his body, surrounding both Nixgut and Zharak in an instant.
Nixgut frowned as this happened.
What was happening?
What was this energy?
What was it doing?
These questions appeared in his mind, but then...
'Meh, if the Lord wanted to hurt me, he would have done it anyway. A mercenary like me isn't worth the effort of an Infinity.'
With that answer, all his questions disappeared. By the time his mind considered the last possibility of the so-called Lord not being the Infinity like he was expecting him to be,
Well, it was already too late by then.
Nux had already devoured the two of them.
And just like that, he now had three Transcendent-Level subordinates. And as his Father-in-Law said, the Universe didn't react this time either.
"That was fun~"
He chuckled as he stared at Marlik, who stood in front of him with his head bowed, being as loyal as ever.
Yes, Nux had used memory manipulation and emotion amplification to turn him into someone absolutely loyal to him, and he was planning to do the same with the other two.
For now, however, his focus was to know more about his Father and the Mission his new subordinates had received.
'Shadow.'
With that thought in his mind, Nux called out. His wife quickly brought him and Marlik back into the Universe, where Zharak and Nixgut were creating a scene.
Of course, Shadow had already teleported them to a random corner, so they couldn't do much even if they wanted to. However, the moment Nux appeared in front of them,
"Lord! Where is this place? And why are all of us... like this?"
Nixgut questioned as he glanced at Nux.
Nux, however, quickly teleported next to them, grabbed their necks, and said,
"Stay still."
He ordered before strange patterns appeared around his body, and he started reading their memories.
The two Transcendents tried to resist, even trying to create their Domains. However, it didn't work. Nux had momentarily taken away their right to form their Domains.
"What is..."
Nixgut, of course, couldn't understand what was happening.
The more aggressive Zharak, on the other hand, tried to cut Nux with his claws, but the claws he was so proud of did nothing to Nux's body.
"Did you forget? This is my world. You cannot win against me."
Nux, who was done reading their memories, grinned at them. Then, he took their storage necklaces, took the artifact he wanted, and said,
"Be good. I'll be back and deal with the two of you."
He disappeared, returned to the main Universe, and activated the Artifact.
[Where is he?]
A familiar voice came from the Artifact when his call was answered. Hearing that voice, Nux's grin widened.
"Hello, Father.
It is your filial son.
Did you miss me?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1961 There is no going back now.
paragraphs: [Where is he?]
A familiar voice came from the Artifact when Nux's call was answered, and the instant Nux heard that voice, his grin widened.
"Hello, Father."
He replied, his grin widening even further as he introduced himself politely.
"It is your filial son.
Did you miss me?"
There was no answer for a moment.
"Hmm? Can you not recognize your own Soul Son? And here I thought the Bond of Soul was stronger than the Bond of Blood.
That makes me quite sad. I foolishly thought you were my only family in this wretched world."
Nux pouted.
Nux's Father, Zylarith Chaosveil, muttered in a low voice, and Nux grinned even further.
"I knew you remembered me. Why would you send people to protect me if you didn't? Clearly, your love for me knows no bounds.
You saved me even when you were so far away, surrounded with riches. How can I not be touched by this?
Even if the threat you saved me from was sent by you in the first place."
Nux's tone suddenly changed.
Yes, that was the mission Nixgut and Zharak received.
Mission Damsel in Distress.

They were required to hire a mercenary who would go after the Leander Family while they were on their mission. Their husband, Nux Leander, would come and protect them, but he would be helpless against a Transcendence Stage Being, Marlik.

Marlik would then kill one or more of his wives to raise the stakes even further, and once the stakes were high enough, two of his 'father's men' would appear and protect him and his wives and take them to safety.
[I did what had to be done.]
Zylarith answered.
"Right, of course.
I am sure you had all the reason in the world to try and kill one or more of my wives, whom you know I love more than myself."
Nux nodded continuously, completely agreeing with his father.
[You are too naïve.]
Zylarith started.
[You still think this Universe revolves around you just because I gave you the system that made you better than others around you.

You are conceited. You do not think before you act, and you love those wives of yours too much. It is an apparent weakness that your enemies can and will take advantage of. Understand this, son, the more you love something, the quicker this Universe will take it away from you.
I was merely trying to show you the reality you have been avoiding all this while, to put you on the right path, a path to greatness, a path that is already set in stone for you,
A path you merely have to close your eyes and walk on.]
Zylarith explained, and seeing that Nux still remained silent, he continued,

[The Universe is Cruel, Nux. The only way to truly get what you want is to stand on top of it, just like how I told you to. However, if you remain as you are, you will never achieve that. There is still time. Come under my protection, and I will guide you. I will protect you, to make sure you and your wives are safe.]
"You are going to protect me?"
Nux raised his eyebrow.
[I will.
That Vampire is asleep again. What do you think will happen if a stronger cultivator came after you? Who will protect you this time if not me?]
"Certainly it wouldn't be those mercenaries you sent. They were quite weak."
Nux chuckled.
Zylarith turned silent.
"And you didn't exactly show off your ability to protect people when you didn't come help those poor lads even when they activated all the Call Artifacts they had to call you.
I gave them more than enough chance to call for reinforcements before I killed them, you know? But you never appeared.
Not a very compelling case, even if I do say so myself."
Nux chuckled.
[You... killed them?]
"Well, they did try to hurt my wives."
Nux answered as if it was the obvious thing to do.
[Who is helping you?]
"Do you truly think I need help dealing with some Transcendent Level Mercenaries? Your expectations of me disappoint me."
[Don't try to fool me. You shouldn't be a Transcendent yet.]
Zylarith quickly denied the possibility.
"Hmm? Did you forget what Power I have? You were the one who gave it to me, you know?
I had to work quite hard to get where I am today."
Zylarith's tone changed. For the first time during this conversation, he seemed... shocked, dumbfounded even.
Nux carefully observed his father's reaction, but then, he sensed the space around him tremble, and his grin widened.
"Whoever you sent won't be able to find me, you know?"
[...what are you talking about?]
"Come on, Father.
You don't have to lie to your son.
Especially when you are so pathetically outmatched."
Nux laughed.
"Stop trying to trace the Artifact's dimensions. You will not find anything. The Space Dimensions around me aren't something anyone around you would ever understand."
Then, he stepped forward and disappeared, appearing inside a certain planet. Even though he stood right in front of the world's netizen, he couldn't see him.
After all, he was hiding in a different dimension. Vulpiana may have gone away from his life, but her Law, however, was still very much useful.
[Where are you?]
Zylarith questioned directly.
"You were the one who wanted to protect me, didn't you? How will you protect me if you don't even know where I am?"
[Don't play games with me, boy.]
Zylarith threatened, his voice turning cold. It looked like he was getting more and more desperate.
Nux, on the other hand, grabbed a Sovereign in front of him and started reading his memories. Of course, he never stopped conversing.
Keeping his father waiting for his answer would be rude, would it not?
Nux was a well-mannered and filial son.
"The game already started the moment you targeted my wives, Zylarith Chaosveil.
There is no going back now."
Nux replied, his golden eyes turning cold as he killed the Sovereign in front of him, devoured his body, and teleported away, appearing in front of another Sovereign and started reading his memories.
