chapters.title: Chapter 1971 Let’s start with a bath, shall we?
paragraphs: "It sure looks happy."
Nux chuckled as he saw how the Universe reacted. The rest of his wives smiled as well. Then suddenly,
"It went better than what he was expecting."
Faustina, who returned to their Universe, spoke with a light smile on her face.
"Mother."
Nux greeted her with a smile on his face.
"The Universe is quite satisfied. It thinks that the anomaly's gone. It has been a while since I have seen Azriel smile like that."
Faustina reported, and Aeliana smiled at those words.
"How did you even come up with that plan?"
Amaya, on the other hand, questioned with a curious look on her face.
"I didn't. It was Azriel."
Faustina answered.

"He could now see everything with the Universe's eyes, so when he stared at us, he realized that in the Universe's eyes, we and Nux had no difference - we are all Anomalies from different Universes. We have no traces of our prior selves left.
So he decided to use it. This was also the reason why he didn't tell you to stop even when the Universe was enraged - he wanted the Universe to become desperate."
"Huh? Why is that? He could have directly devoured an Anomaly instead, couldn't he?"
Skyla didn't understand and tilted her head in confusion.
"The higher the desperation, the higher the dependency."
Amaya answered as she turned toward her sister, and Faustina nodded at those words.
"The goal wasn't to help the Universe, it was to make it more dependable on Azriel.
The Universe has tried to get rid of the anomaly tens of times but never once was it able to catch it, or even harm it for that regard.

The Anomaly had always been playing around with the Universe, mocking it at every step, yet the Hero was able to take care of this Anomaly in their second encounter. This showed how dependable the Hero was.
This showed how capable the Hero was."
"But the Universe chose Lord Azriel because it knew how capable he was, didn't it? It should already know that - Lord Azriel was the best option he had."
Skyla muttered.

"Knowing and believing are two different things. Yes, the Hero was young, his journey had only begun, and the Universe would have understood if the Hero was unable to catch the Anomaly. But if the Hero did manage to get rid of the anomaly...
Imagine how quickly would the Hero's importance increase."
Faustina answered.
"Wouldn't it be dangerous instead?"
Suddenly, Vyriana questioned.
"Now that the Anomaly's gone, wouldn't the Universe think that the Hero isn't needed anymore?"
"It might."
Faustina didn't deny it.
"The Anomaly isn't gone yet."
Nux completed his mother's sentence.
Faustina nodded,

"The instant the Universe even thinks of getting rid of the Anomaly, you will go and devour another World again. That would be the appearance of the Second Anomaly, then the Third, the Fourth, the Fifth, and more and more.
The Universe will soon be at War with the Anomalies, and to win this War, it would need its child at its strongest.
This will ensure Azriel's survival."
Faustina smiled as she said those words.
She was definitely liking this little game.
Aeliana was the same - the more the Universe relied on her father, the more relieved she felt.
"Hehe, it is like we are playing both the good guys and the bad guys in a stage show."
Skyla laughed as she thought about it. The rest chuckled at those words.
"So mother, why are you here?"
Nux questioned.
"I wanted to tell you to lay low for a while, stop your investigation. Or at the very least, you cannot devour another entity from the Main Universe and alert him."
"For how long?"
"A few months."
"Why is that?"
"Wouldn't it be strange if the second Anomaly appeared right after one was dead? Also, the Anomaly had never appeared so frequently before - don't break that right now, right after Yrniel is gone."
"I understand."
Nux nodded.
"This would have been so much simpler if Lord Azriel could have told us about the Temple of Time."
Amaya shook her head.

This was something she had thought of before - since Azriel was now connected to the Universe, if he wanted, he could search for Temple of Time using this connection. The problem with this plan, however, was that none of them knew what sort of place this Temple of Time was.
If they were forced to devour something there - which would probably happen, then the Universe would realize that the Anomaly appeared there.
For the enemy to appear in a place the Hero was looking into - that would be too suspicious.
In the end, they had to do this themselves.
Faustina knew that as well, so she just shook her head with a wry smile on her face.
"You can still investigate as long as the Universe does not know of it."
"It is alright."
Nux shrugged.
"We have all the time in the world."
He then stretched his body and stared at his mother.
"I was also thinking of getting some rest.
Are you going to stay?"
"No, I will return."
"I will miss you."
Nux nodded as he hugged his mother. Aeliana hugged Faustina as well, then, the Human Progenitor turned toward Shadow, and the woman sent her away.
"Haaaahhhh..."
The instant his mother disappeared, a smile appeared on Nux's face as he turned toward his wives.
Then, he grinned,
"We have a few months to ourselves - any ideas as to what we might do?"
The women grinned.
Clearly, all of them had their own plans for these next few months.
"Alright, there is no need to fight. According to the rules, it should be my turn now."
Very quickly, Allura stepped forward and announced her claims.
"What rules?"
Thyra narrowed her eyes.
She was especially resistant to these rules because her turn was at the very last.
"Of course, you would say that when you already enjoyed the privileges of these rules and are now at a disadvantage."
Allura snorted as she appeared next to Nux.
"I am telling this right now - it is my turn. There will be no change in the rules. The new additions will be added accordingly."
The Succubus spoke as she stared at Aeliana and Eisheth.

Amaya, on the other hand, had already surrounded herself and Vyriana with Devouring Mist and devoured time around them. Nux will wake them up when it was their turn - it would be like instantly skipping to their turn.
This was also the reason Amaya had become much more tolerable to all these annoying bitches around her - she could devour time around herself and only be awake when her Nux was with her.
She helped Vyriana because the Dragon wanted the same. The rest of her sisters still needed to break through to the Primordial Stage, so she didn't help them.
As for Aeliana...
Why should she help that bitch?
Yes, the Devourer wasn't a fan of the Vampire.
Not that the Vampire needed her - she simply closed her eyes and started cultivating. She had different ambitions.
She wanted to break through to the Transcendent Phase.
Now that Yrniel was no longer limiting her, it was high time that she broke through, and once she did...
She would deal with the devourer on her own.

Yes, the Vampire hadn't forgotten how the Devourer had hogged HER Nux all for herself when she broke through. She still remembered how she surrounded every single one of them with that devouring mist of hers.
If only she wasn't weakened back then, she would have shown her the consequences. But no matter.
The Vampire still had time.
The moment she breaks through and becomes a Transcendent will be the moment when she will put the devourer in her place.
Yes, the Vampire now had an entirely new motivation to break through.

Nux, who could sense what the two women were thinking, couldn't help but laugh out loud. As dangerous as their rivalry was getting, it was also pushing them further, making them stronger and stronger.
Because of them, women like Vyriana and Astaria pushed themselves beyond the limits as well, and because of them, Ember, Thyra, and others forced themselves to cultivate and break through as well.
The race between the harem was on.
Since the reward for a breakthrough was direct time with Nux without having to use their turn, none of the women backed down.
Nux enjoyed this competition - after all, no matter who won, the true victor would be him.

He felt like he was the income tax department back on Earth who charged taxes on the tournament prizes - it didn't matter who the winner was, the true victor would always be the government of the people.
'Hahaha~'
Nux laughed at his own joke as his eyes fell on his Allura, who was floating toward him with that sensual, hypnotizing smile on her face.
Something that he couldn't resist no matter how hard he tried.
"Are you ready?"
The woman whispered into his ears as a chill of anticipation ran through his body.

He nodded lightly, his body trembling ever so slightly like prey standing near its predator. Allura's grin widened. Very quickly, the two of them were covered in shadows and appeared in a dead world that had long become their new home.
As safe as their own Universe was, Nux wanted to see all of his wives whenever he spent time with them - not their shadow versions.
So he preferred doing the deed outside.
As safe as their own Universe was, Nux wanted to see all of his wives whenever he spent time with them - not their shadow versions.
So he preferred doing the deed outside.
"Let's start with a bath, shall we?"
Allura muttered as she gently tapped onto Nux's chest and took him to the bathroom. There, she removed his clothes and took him inside the bathtub, and then,
"I'll be back."
She muttered as she walked out.
Nux didn't know what she was preparing - he had stopped sensing her emotions to make it more fun. His anticipation made his little brother twitch.
Click
Then, he heard the doors open again.
Step Step
The footsteps echoed in the bathroom. Soon, however, a frown appeared on Nux's face.
This didn't... sound like Allura's footsteps...
It belonged to someone else.

Nux whispered into Lyriana's ears in a voice so sensual that she felt strange a jolt of pleasure running all over her body.
After a long long while, she felt... weak.
And what's worse was that... her body didn't hate this weakness.
Yes, she, Lyriana Frostwillow, who left her everything, her family, her Kingdom, her World, and even her lovely daughter, to pursue strength, didn't hate it when her body felt weak...
It was strange.
It was inexplicable.
Nux's embrace felt... a little too comfortable.
'I-Is this what those women feel...?'
Lyriana wondered in her head, as she automatically closed her eyes. The comfort she felt was too strong for her to resist.
'No wonder they lose their minds when he is not around...
They are all a bunch of addicts.'
The Former Queen finally realized.
Nux was the drug those women craved, a drug every woman should avoid, no matter how enticing it felt.

He may be the most handsome man they ever laid their eyes upon, he may be the most caring being one could find, he may be the one who would make you feel that you can finally let go of everything you have been hiding all this while,
But...
One should not, at any cost, get close to him.
Everything he provides, everything he gives, comes with a great cost,
An Eternity of Dependence.
He would make you a slave to this comforting, loving addiction and you will lose yourselves.
Just like...
How she was currently losing herself...

The moment Lyriana realized it, her eyes sprung open. She tried to move away, yet her weak body couldn't do anything. The only thing that moved was the water she spilled because of her sudden movement.
Then, she heard that eerie, weakening voice again,
"You didn't answer my question, Lyriana."
Every time this man whispered into her ears, Lyriana felt like his voice was directly entering her brain and taking over it. It felt... scary.
Especially when Lyriana realized that she was unable to form an answer to his question.
What held her back?
Nothing.
No answer came to her mind, nothing was holding her back from falling into this cycle of addiction,
Her heart... it willingly wanted her to fall for this trap.
Something that the last bit of her sanity denied with every core of its being, very quickly, her mind came up with a viable excuse.
"I... I had a husband."
At least it sounded more viable in her head, but...
"And?"
Nux simply continued to whisper into her ears, his lips lightly touching her long ears, sending strange tremors throughout her body.

paragraphs: The Elven Queen was so confused that in the end, she decided to directly ask the man himself and the answer she got was something she couldn't forget,
"I love her."
What a foolish answer.
Lyriana wanted to laugh out loud but...
Seeing that look in that man's eyes when he talked about his wife...
Lyriana couldn't laugh.
That look... she never saw something like that in her life.
And it made her feel strange, after all, the boy in front of her was barely a few hundred years old, how could... he have a look on his face that she couldn't understand?
Even if one calls him a naïve little body who let his hormones get the better of him... this... still didn't make sense.
Something was wrong.
And it wasn't just him, those wives of his were the same.

Every single one of them had the same look in their eyes, it was absurd, it was... intriguing. Curious and wanting to understand that look, Lyriana started following the boy more than he had to. Yes, there were times when she saw things she didn't wish to see, things that should have been kept private, but she didn't stop. And it was a mistake.
Her body, which had long stopped feeling any form of desire, finally felt... something.
She didn't sense it, she was too busy trying to understand that look, but her body started changing.
Fortunately, the Boy didn't stay for long.

He won the war everyone thought he would lose and he freed her and her people, leaving them alone, he even expressed his gratitude and apologized for doing what he did. Because of the Elven Kingdom's relationship with him, theElven Kingdom became even stronger, surpassing even the Blood Kingdom in some regards.
But the Boy had disappeared, disappeared into a grander world.
Lyriana was left alone and honestly, it would have been better for the elf if this continued, but...
A few centuries later, the boy reappeared and kidnapped her.
He showed her a world she had never seen before, things she couldn't even comprehend, power levels that simply felt like a fantasy and in an instant, the strength craving Lyriana was captivated.
She decided to abandon everything and come with the boy, who now seemed to have turned into quite a fine man, much more powerful than her or any other being she knew.
A man who seemed... quite attractive.
But again, her mind never understood how her heart was slowly losing itself.
What's worse?
A few years later, she made a foolish mistake of severing herself and becoming connected to this man, for eternity.
Now, things became even worse, she was now able to sense the man's thoughts any time she desired, she could now peek into the man's mind and her curiosity took the better of her.
Still wanting to understand that look and whether what he said about his wives was indeed the truth, she started sensing his emotions.
And then it happened.
The instant she tried it, her mind was overwhelmed with such a strong love that she couldn't even believe that it was real.
The outright craziness, the feeling of possessiveness, the need to always be in their presence, Lyriana could sense it all. It was so suffocating and in no way healthy, yet...
She... she started to like this feeling.
The only problem was... that this feeling wasn't directed at her.
It was directed at those women—women who had lost their minds and directed the same feeling at him.
Lyriana... turned into a spectator.

She saw every time the man and his wives were together, she sensed the heavy love Nux had for his wives, love that couldn't be described with words, she sensed every single emotion, so very much that she...
She felt envious.
She always wanted to explore the vast world, the vast Universe now, she wanted to see everything there was but...

These people were completely opposite, they were satisfied with each other's presence, as if they were each other's world. The only reason these people even bothered getting stronger was so that they could explore it together and be safe.
It was such a strange thought process and yet...
It made the most sense.
What made things even worse was that now she couldn't stop sensing Nux's emotions. So every time he was with his wives and his already strong emotions get even stronger, it affects her mind as well.
She doesn't just become a spectator, she feels everything that happens in a certain way, and with her body that had now started to feel desire again, things became even more complicated for her.
Her heart knew what she desired, but her mind had so much control over her heart that it couldn't express what it wanted and was in constant, silent pain.
At least that was the case till just a few moments ago,
But now...
"Did you love your husband?"
But now that all these heavy emotions were directed at her, her heart's desire got much stronger than before.
It wasn't just her heart, her body itself had started moving, her desire had now reached its peak, it was now her heart and body against her mind.
And with Nux's words constantly weakening her mind, it wasn't exactly a fair battle.
"H-He was still my husband."
"That is not the answer to my question, Lyriana."
Lyriana momentarily turned silent.
Her mind raced and she finally came up with a strong answer,
"Do you think your wives will ever find another man if something happens to you?"
"My wives love me."
Nux's answer was instantaneous. Then, he tightened his hug around the woman and,
"Did you love your husband as much as my wives love me?"
Lyriana turned silent at that question, the answer couldn't be clearer, for both her mind and her heart.
Then suddenly, Nux asked a strange question.
"Do you like this?"
The Former Queen frowned, she turned her head towards Nux with a frown,
"Like wha-"
She wanted to ask a question but then,
Nux sealed her lips.

"W-W-Wha- Annh~"

Her body trembled again.
Her ears were too sensitive.
Once Nux was satisfied devouring her ear, he moved away again, allowing the woman to breathe a little. Slowly, she opened her eyes and saw Nux staring at her with a light, gentle smile on his face.
Waiting for her to answer his question.

"Do you like this?"

He gave her a peck again, then again, and then again.

"Do you like this?"

"When I kiss you like this?"
He muttered as he kissed her forehead again.
"Do you crave more of this?"
He questioned as he kissed her right below her lips.
"Does your heart skip a beat when I do this?"
He asked when he kissed her lips again, then, he moved towards her ear again and continued his demonic whispers.
"Do you... lose yourself when I do this?
Don't worry, you don't have to answer."
Suddenly, he spoke up.
"I already know the answer."
He smiled as he looked down at her body,
"I know you already lost yourself long ago."
He grinned and when Lyriana followed his gaze to understand what he was talking about, her eyes widened in shock when she realized that the water they were in was frozen,
Sealing their body together.

chapters.title: Chapter 1981 If only I wasn’t stuck at the Emperor Stage.
paragraphs: A man, sitting cross-legged, was hovering in outer space, drifting in the distant void that no one knew of, without a care for all the poisonous Universal Energy that surrounded him. Yes, it was the previous Vampire Progenitor, Azriel.

After the Anomaly was dead, he, the Universe's Child, wasn't discarded by the Universe. Rather, he once again returned to the edge of the Universe, where no one would disturb him, and he continued cultivating.

In the past year, however, he had only managed to reach the Emperor Stage, barely breaking through Phase One of cultivation. Of course, for others, this progress was nothing short of absurd, but Azriel was different.

For Azriel, understanding his new Cultivation Bridge was never difficult. He barely needed a few hours to understand the next stage, and all he needed to do was absorb enough Universal Energy and break through.
This was also the reason he became an Expert Stage Cultivator from a mortal in a matter of days.

Even now, when he broke through the Emperor Stage three months ago, he had already understood his future path to Sage within six hours, and for the past three months, he had been constantly absorbing more and more Universal Energy but was still far from breaking through to the Sage Stage.

Yes, his cultivation rate had slowed down. The rate at which he was able to absorb Universal Energy had slowed down—drastically at that. Strangely, all of this happened right after the Anomaly was dead.

Weirdly enough, it wasn't just his Universal Energy absorption rate that had slowed down. His connection with the Universe's Will was somewhat weakened as well. He was unable to understand its thoughts as clearly as he could before, and because of that, while he still had the power to use the Universe's help to devour an entity like before, since the communication between them had weakened, he now needed much more time to form that connection and convince the Universe to use its power.

Yes, very weird indeed—almost as if the Universe, even though it had not discarded its child, was trying to slow down his progress. There could be various reasons why that was the case. Maybe the Universe wanted to keep its freedom for a little longer before finally sharing its power with someone else, or maybe it didn't need him anymore now that the Anomaly was gone.

Of course, Azriel knew all of this wasn't true. The Universe was his ally, and he was its ally. Their relationship was special. They had no reason to try and sabotage each other. All of these were merely anger-inducing thoughts that he needed to get rid of, and he needed to think of the Universe as his closest ally.
Deep in his heart, Azriel knew all this would stop, that his ally would soon deal with whatever problem was slowing him down, and his usual cultivation speed would return soon.
Actually, he was quite sure about that.
So he continued to cultivate tirelessly, absorbing the Universal Energy, slowly but surely moving towards the next stage. But then,
His brows twitched.
"What...?"
He opened his eyes with a frown on his face.
"But that isn't possible. I killed him myself. You sensed it as well."
He answered. His tone sounded like he was trying to calm someone down.

"Yes, I understand that someone stole another Middle-Level World of ours, but I am telling you that isn't possible! That someone who had the ability to do that is already dead. We killed him together. There must have been a mista—"
Before Azriel could even complete his words,
Bzzzz
The very space around him trembled.
Almost as if the entity he was talking to was enraged and saying,
'You think I would make a mistake like that?'
In an instant, Azriel turned silent, his expression grim.
"So what you are trying to say is that... the Anomaly is back?
After you killed it yourself?"
Azriel questioned in a solemn tone.
"Is that not absurd? If even you cannot get rid of him, doesn't this mean he is invincible?"

This time, the Universe didn't reply. It was silent, and while Azriel still couldn't understand what it was thinking because of their weakened connection, he, even in this state, knew that his friend and their connection would be back.
After all, strong friendships like theirs were hard to break.
Suddenly, another thought appeared in Azriel's head.
"What if... he isn't the Anomaly we killed but another Anomaly?
A Second Anomaly."
In an instant, the despairing Universe stopped, as if Azriel's thought had lit up a new ray of hope. In an instant, it gave orders.
"You want me to... go and devour it again?"
Azriel frowned.
"No, I understand that I will be able to tell whether it is indeed a Second Anomaly or not, but..."
The previous Vampire Progenitor thought for a moment and then,
"Alright, I will go."
He nodded.
He needed to help his friend, after all. That was what friends were for, wasn't it?
With that thought in his mind, Azriel allowed the Universe to dematerialize and materialize him next to the Middle-Level World that had just been devoured.
The moment Azriel appeared, he stared at the void ahead of him and started looking around.
"I do not see anything."
He spoke out loud.
"I guess we would need to wait like we did the last time.
It is a team effort, eh?"
He chuckled lightly. He liked the feeling of helping his friend.
Soon, the Universe noticed another disappearance. This time, it was three Transcendent Level Beings from another Middle-Level World.
"Take me there."
Azriel ordered when the Universe informed him, and the Universe materialized him in the world where this had happened.

There, Azriel's eyes fell on a shadowy figure, who was holding the World's Will in his hand. The figure seemed somewhat similar to the Anomaly they had killed before, but their body structure, their face, and even their ability seemed different.

He is the Second Anomaly."
Azriel commented.

The Anomaly disappeared.

sentences.text: A man, sitting cross-legged, was hovering in outer space, drifting in the distant void that no one knew of, without a care for all the poisonous Universal Energy that surrounded him.
Yes, it was the previous Vampire Progenitor, Azriel.
After the Anomaly was dead, he, the Universe's Child, wasn't discarded by the Universe.
Rather, he once again returned to the edge of the Universe, where no one would disturb him, and he continued cultivating.
In the past year, however, he had only managed to reach the Emperor Stage, barely breaking through Phase One of cultivation.
Of course, for others, this progress was nothing short of absurd, but Azriel was different.
For Azriel, understanding his new Cultivation Bridge was never difficult.
He barely needed a few hours to understand the next stage, and all he needed to do was absorb enough Universal Energy and break through.
This was also the reason he became an Expert Stage Cultivator from a mortal in a matter of days.

Even now, when he broke through the Emperor Stage three months ago, he had already understood his future path to Sage within six hours, and for the past three months, he had been constantly absorbing more and more Universal Energy but was still far from breaking through to the Sage Stage.
Yes, his cultivation rate had slowed down.
The rate at which he was able to absorb Universal Energy had slowed down—drastically at that.
Strangely, all of this happened right after the Anomaly was dead.
Weirdly enough, it wasn't just his Universal Energy absorption rate that had slowed down.
His connection with the Universe's Will was somewhat weakened as well.

He was unable to understand its thoughts as clearly as he could before, and because of that, while he still had the power to use the Universe's help to devour an entity like before, since the communication between them had weakened, he now needed much more time to form that connection and convince the Universe to use its power.
Yes, very weird indeed—almost as if the Universe, even though it had not discarded its child, was trying to slow down his progress.
There could be various reasons why that was the case.
Maybe the Universe wanted to keep its freedom for a little longer before finally sharing its power with someone else, or maybe it didn't need him anymore now that the Anomaly was gone.
Of course, Azriel knew all of this wasn't true.
The Universe was his ally, and he was its ally.
Their relationship was special.
They had no reason to try and sabotage each other.
All of these were merely anger-inducing thoughts that he needed to get rid of, and he needed to think of the Universe as his closest ally.
Deep in his heart, Azriel knew all this would stop, that his ally would soon deal with whatever problem was slowing him down, and his usual cultivation speed would return soon.
Actually, he was quite sure about that.
So he continued to cultivate tirelessly, absorbing the Universal Energy, slowly but surely moving towards the next stage.
But then,
His brows twitched.
"What...?"
He opened his eyes with a frown on his face.
"But that isn't possible.
I killed him myself.
You sensed it as well."
He answered.
His tone sounded like he was trying to calm someone down.
"Yes, I understand that someone stole another Middle-Level World of ours, but I am telling you that isn't possible!
That someone who had the ability to do that is already dead.
We killed him together.
There must have been a mista—"
Before Azriel could even complete his words,
Bzzzz
The very space around him trembled.
Almost as if the entity he was talking to was enraged and saying,
'You think I would make a mistake like that?'
In an instant, Azriel turned silent, his expression grim.
"So what you are trying to say is that... the Anomaly is back?
After you killed it yourself?"
Azriel questioned in a solemn tone.
"Is that not absurd?
If even you cannot get rid of him, doesn't this mean he is invincible?"
This time, the Universe didn't reply.
It was silent, and while Azriel still couldn't understand what it was thinking because of their weakened connection, he, even in this state, knew that his friend and their connection would be back.
After all, strong friendships like theirs were hard to break.

"What if... he isn't the Anomaly we killed but another Anomaly?
A Second Anomaly."

In an instant, it gave orders.
"You want me to... go and devour it again?"
Azriel frowned.
"No, I understand that I will be able to tell whether it is indeed a Second Anomaly or not, but..."

"Alright, I will go."
He nodded.

The Anomaly disappeared.

If only I wasn't stuck at the Emperor Stage."

paragraphs: "It appeared again."
Azriel exhaled, his fists clenching. His crimson eyes glowed with a sharp, calculating light.
The Anomaly—this time, he wouldn't let it escape, no matter what.
"Where?"
He questioned out loud, preparing himself to face the enemy. He knew the Universe would teleport him the instant the Anomaly devoured a being.
And just as he expected, suddenly, the space around him turned, and he dematerialized, materializing in yet another world.
He looked around. Once again, he tried to find it—the being who had been making his life a living hell all this while.
Right now, he was in what seemed like an empty throne room.
"I don't see anyone."
He spoke out loud as he expanded his senses. Then, he rushed forward into a room right behind the throne room, and there he was.
The Anomaly.
Azriel's heart pounded. He raised his hand to point—
—And it was gone.
It happened again.

The moment he appeared, the Anomaly had already sensed his presence. The thing's reaction speed was far stronger than Azriel's. If Azriel were as strong as he once was, maybe it wouldn't have been a problem, but with him just being an Emperor, it was far more difficult.
Before his finger had even moved, the Anomaly had already escaped.
"It's gone..."
Azriel muttered. His voice was indeed low, but it was full of so much frustration and hate that even he couldn't believe it.
This Anomaly—he hated this thing to his very core!
However, before he could lose himself in hate, the Universe called out again. He gritted his teeth as he prepared himself, and once again, Azriel's body was materialized into another world.
This time, it was a war zone. It seemed like he was near a general's camp.
"Who are you?"
One of the soldiers patrolling the area sensed his presence, instantly calling the rest of the patrol party.
Azriel was surrounded.
"State your name, race, and purpose for coming here."
The soldier ordered.
"Fuck."
Azriel cursed in his head. He wanted to thwart these soldiers away and find the Anomaly, but these soldiers were all Sovereigns. He, as an Emperor, was no match for them.
In the end—
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
The world trembled. Yes, the Anomaly had begun devouring this world.
"Get out of my wa—"
Azriel shouted, wanting to rush toward the Anomaly and see where he was so he could stop him, but—
BOOOOOM
The soldiers in front of him used their Aura, instantly suppressing him. An Emperor like him could never possibly resist the Aura of a Sovereign.
"What did you do!?"
One of the soldiers shouted, instantly blaming Azriel. He was prepared to capture Azriel, but suddenly—
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
The world trembled again, and no, this time, it wasn't because of the world's will—the Universe itself was reacting.
Since he couldn't devour the Anomaly, he would get rid of the whole world together with the Anomaly, like he had done before.
But it was already too late.
The Anomaly managed to devour the world, and before the Universe could even attack, the world, together with the soldiers surrounding Azriel, crumbled into nothingness.
Azriel, who now knelt in the void, hovering aimlessly, lowered his head, cursing himself for being so weak.
This time, they didn't just lose a single entity—they lost an entire world.

More time passed. Around thirty minutes later, the Anomaly devoured another being. Once again, Azriel was materialized into a new world. This time, he managed to find the Anomaly, but the Anomaly found him as well.
Yes, the Anomaly disappeared again.
Azriel failed again.
It was the third time.
Then the fourth.
The fifth.
And sixth.

Again and again, Azriel was thrown all across the Universe, placed in front of the Anomaly mere moments after it had fed. And every time, before the previous Vampire Progenitor—the once strongest being in this Universe—could even react, before he could even begin to point at the Anomaly, it escaped.
It was too fast.
Too elusive.
Too... impossible.
And Azriel—he... was too weak.
He hovered in the void, with his head low, as if he had lost everything. His eyes, however, were still determined.
He wanted to catch him—that Anomaly—and this time, he would not fail!
The Universe's Child waited for the Anomaly to appear again as he prepared himself.
Minutes, hours, days, even weeks passed by...
But the Anomaly didn't appear.
Yes, it was gone.
And no, it wasn't gone. It had just... disappeared.
It had... escaped.
Yes, Azriel failed.
He lowered his head, his fists trembling. The silence around him now felt suffocating.
His throat felt dry, his voice barely sounded like a whisper.
"If only I had cultivated more...
If only I had absorbed more Universal Energy...
If I were just faster... just stronger..."
He clenched his jaw. The reality was unbearable. If he had been stronger—if he had trained harder—the Anomaly wouldn't have escaped.
The Universe's Will did not respond.
It did not comfort him.
It did not offer him encouragement.
It remained silent.
"Take me back."
Suddenly, Azriel spoke up. The Universe's Will did what he said and materialized him back at the edge of the Universe, where he sat down and started cultivating again.

He wanted to get stronger so he could take revenge. He wanted to get even with that thing and destroy it. Even if he couldn't absorb the Universal Energy as fast as he used to, he still wouldn't give up.
He would continue to work hard, and he would continue until he finally got rid of it.
And just while Azriel was thinking all this—
Whoosh Whoosh Whoosh

Suddenly, out of nowhere, the amount of Universal Energy he was able to absorb became higher and higher. Not only that, Azriel realized that his connection with the Universe had become stronger as well—just like how it was before.
And the moment all of that happened...
The frustrated and despairing look on Azriel's face disappeared, and the previous Vampire Progenitor smirked.
Just as he expected, his friend had finally solved whatever problem it was facing and was now back.
Their friendship was indeed the strongest.

chapters.title: Chapter 1983 I am sure you have a better way, don’t you?
paragraphs: "The Universe returned to its child again.
Azriel's connection with the Universe is back to normal, his cultivation speed has increased, and everything is going just as we expected."
Faustina reported with a smirk.
"That didn't take long."
Aeliana chuckled.
"The Second Anomaly did escape because the Universe's Child wasn't strong enough. If the Universe wasn't trying to keep him under check for the past year, this might not have happened."
Faustina laughed, and the rest of the women laughed as well.
But Nux didn't.
"At least someone's getting what they were expecting."
He sighed, instantly attracting the women's attention.
"Still nothing?"
Amaya frowned.
Nux shook his head.
"All basic information, these worlds knew about Chronoxis and the fact that Orynthar attacked Chronoxis, but none of them bothered to learn why they did it.
They just... felt it was normal for a High-Level World to prey on a Middle-Level World, which isn't exactly wrong. Chronoxis wasn't the first Middle-Level world Orynthar attacked and destroyed."
He answered.
"So we have nothing...?"
Felberta questioned, and Nux's face turned grim.
"There is one lead..."
"A lead...?"

"All the Middle-Level Worlds I devoured told me about one world, Orynthar's closest ally, the world that took Orynthar's position after Lord Azriel destroyed it, Tenebris. If Chronoxis or the Temple of Time was of any importance to Orynthar, Tenebris should know it."
"If we have the target, then what are we waiting for?"
Astaria questioned as she clenched her sword, prepared to jump into battle for her husband's sake.
Aeliana, however, had a solemn look on her face.
"If it took Orynthar's position then..."
"It is a High-Level World."
Nux completed the Vampire's sentence, and in an instant, the women's faces turned grim.
"And Eternals..."
Astaria glanced at Nux, and he shook his head.
"We cannot defeat them, even with the Army of Transcendents we have."
Eternals were different, they were a threat to Nux and his wives, he couldn't risk it. This was the entire reason he wasn't going after his father yet.
"What if... we do not have to face an Eternal?"
Suddenly, Amaya questioned.
"We need to devour Tenebris, you think its leader would sit back and let us do it without making a move?"
Thyra questioned back.
Nux, on the other hand, stared at his wife, letting her continue.

"What we need is information, correct? Devouring Tenebris isn't the only way to get what we want, is it? It is just a convenience we use because of how efficient it is, normal people do not have such convenience, yet they are still able to get the information they want.
There are still ways to get information without having to destroy a world."
The women narrowed their eyes at the Devourer's words.
"What are you planning?"
Aeliana questioned.
"Eternals are called Eternals because they can live for Eternity, can they not?"
Nux nodded at her question.
"Then the Eternals leading Tenebris should be alive when Orynthar attacked Chronoxis, they should know why Orynthar did it."
"They should."
Nux nodded.

According to the memories of the worlds he devoured, the Leaders of Tenebris haven't changed for hundreds of thousands of years now. They were present when Orynthar existed, and they are still alive and well.
"Then why don't we just ask them? If it is something important, I am sure they know about it."
"And what's the grand plan? Ask them nicely?"
Vyriana questioned.
"We will threaten them."
"Threaten... the Eternals?"
The women raised their eyebrows, Nux on the other hand, could guess what Amaya was thinking about.
"It doesn't have to be the Eternals, everyone has something they want, if we give them what they want..."
"If we were capable of giving an Eternal something he couldn't take on his own, we wouldn't have to worry about things we usually do."
"There are things people cannot get even if they have all the power in the world."
Amaya answered, and Nux grinned at those words. A similar grin appeared on Amaya's face as she turned back towards Nux and,
"How many Eternals are there in Tenebris?"
"It is one of the stronger High-Level Worlds, so four."
Nux answered.

"All we need to do is to find out everything we can about these four. Kidnap their subordinates, their closest allies, their enemies, their kin, kidnap everyone, read all their memories, learn every single thing there is to learn about them.
Find their weakness, something that usually holds them back.
Someone they hate, someone they love, something they want, anything of value, anything they cannot get but we can, anything that can be used to trade for the information we want, find it.
I refuse to believe that out of the four of them, not even one would need our help."
"Help?"
Aeliana raised her eyebrow at those words.
"You are planning to kidnap someone they love and get the information as ransom."
"And?"
Amaya simply shrugged.
She glanced at Nux, and her eyes darkened,
"We sacrifice worlds to get what we want, what are the lives of a few more? If it means my Nux gets what he wants, I'll burn the entire Universe if I must."
Seeing that familiar craziness in those eyes, Nux couldn't hide his grin. This is why he loved his Devourer so much. She shared the same craziness he did.
The two crazy fools stared at each other for the next few seconds.
"It won't be easy."
Suddenly, Felberta called out.
"We are practically going against a High-Level World, the closest aides of an Eternal would be Transcendent-Level Beings, and this time, we cannot use the same trick we used before."
The Eldraeth muttered as she glanced at Eisheth and Skyla.
"It can work."
Skyla answered.
"My Law makes it so they do not jump into a fight the moment they see us, while Sister Eisheth's Law makes them wish to submit to her."
Skyla then turned towards Nux and grinned mischievously, like a little child who thought of something evil.
"I am sure you have a better way, don't you?"
Nux grinned at those words.

She glanced at Nux, and her eyes darkened,
"We sacrifice worlds to get what we want, what are the lives of a few more?
If it means my Nux gets what he wants, I'll burn the entire Universe if I must."
Seeing that familiar craziness in those eyes, Nux couldn't hide his grin.
This is why he loved his Devourer so much.
She shared the same craziness he did.
The two crazy fools stared at each other for the next few seconds.
"It won't be easy."
Suddenly, Felberta called out.
"We are practically going against a High-Level World, the closest aides of an Eternal would be Transcendent-Level Beings, and this time, we cannot use the same trick we used before."
The Eldraeth muttered as she glanced at Eisheth and Skyla.
"It can work."
Skyla answered.
"My Law makes it so they do not jump into a fight the moment they see us, while Sister Eisheth's Law makes them wish to submit to her."
Skyla then turned towards Nux and grinned mischievously, like a little child who thought of something evil.
"I am sure you have a better way, don't you?"
Nux grinned at those words.

paragraphs: "Lord Dainar."

A shadowy, crystallized obsidian being materialized into an absurdly large throne room that was made of obsidian metal and knelt in front of the being sitting on the Throne at the very end of the Hall. The being on the throne had features similar to his, just that his body was much darker and had a higher number of horns.
*Picture of the Race*
"Report."
Dainar ordered with a grim look on his face.
"It is Quoril this time."
The being, Rivenar, reported, and the moment he heard those words, Dainar clenched his fists, and the space around him cracked.
"Anything?"
He questioned after calming himself down.
"Nothing."
Rivenar shook his head.
"There was no trace left, no struggles of a fight, no signs of his Law or any of his abilities being used, she just... disappeared."
"This is already the eleventh one."
Dainar commented, and Rivenar lowered his head, not daring to say anything. He knew his Lord was angry.

It all started a few days ago when, one by one, his close subordinates started disappearing without a trace. They tried looking around, but they couldn't find anything. Even when they searched throughout Tenebris for similar cases and scoured through the history books to see if something similar had happened before, they failed to find anything.

They even considered the possibility of the Foreign World being involved, but Dainar shook his head. All the Foreigners were kept in check with Dainar constantly tailing their movements using Tenebris's Will.

The only link between all the disappearances was the fact that all eleven of them were Dainar's kin or subordinates, people who were on his side. It was clearly a targeted campaign, one arranged by Lord Dainar's enemy. The problem, however, was that they didn't know which out of the three of them was responsible for it and how they were doing it.
"Keep this matter to yourself. Make sure it doesn't spread out. We cannot appear weak, not until we find out which one of the three is behind this."
Dainar ordered.
"As you command, my Lord."
Rivenar nodded as he bowed his head.
"You can leave."
He ordered.
Rivenar stood up, but before he left—
"And be very careful. The instant you sense something is wrong, even if it is nothing more than a simple hunch, you activate the artifact and summon me. Is that clear?"
"Yes, my Lord."

Rivenar nodded again. If there was one thing he was confident about, it was his reaction speed. Honestly, he wanted the perpetrator to come after him. At the very least, that would end this long, tiresome search, and he would finally be able to catch him.
Yes, he was that confident.
And... naïve.
Because what he wished for indeed came true.
While he was about to walk into the meeting hall to command his trusted subordinates to set up different traps in order to catch the perpetrator—
He suddenly disappeared.
Yes, the perpetrator didn't come for him. He directly teleported him next to him, just like he did with the others.
"Hu—where am I—?"
Rivenar blinked, unable to believe what had happened to him. He had appeared in outer space, surrounded by nothing but Universal Energy and other Cosmic Entities.

He was teleported away. It was something that made him frown. After all, he had already set up an anti-teleportation field that constantly altered Space Laws all over the castle by Lord Dainar's orders. Let alone teleporting someone else without their permission—even teleporting oneself in or out of that place shouldn't have been possible.

Of course, while he was thinking of all this, his mind didn't stop working. The reaction speed he trusted so much activated to its fullest extent, and he had already activated the artifact that would summon Lord Dainar here. But then—
"Don't bother using Sirecall, Rivenar. It won't work here."
He heard a voice.
"Hu—"
Rivenar tried turning around, but suddenly, a domain was deployed, and ethereal chains grabbed him, instantly taking away his ability to move.
It was only then that he realized it.
He was surrounded. Not by one or two, but thirty-five Transcendents. And if what the voice said about Sirecall—the artifact he had activated—was indeed true, then he was helpless.
And when, a few seconds after activating Sirecall, his Lord Dainar still didn't appear, he realized that he was indeed helpless.
His final bit of resistance disappeared when Obsidian Lock, an artifact created especially to deal with his race and seal their power, was used.

Obsidian Lock was one of the most secretive artifacts in Tenebris. If the enemy knew about it and even had it, then it meant he was already too deep in their ranks. There was no possible way to resist him.
With his spirit broken, Nux didn't have a hard time reading his memories. Once he was done, he teleported him to a place where space stretched endlessly.
Yes, it was a prison he couldn't escape from.
"Did you find anything?"
Amaya questioned.
"The Four Eternals have been alive for more than a million years now."
Nux answered.
"They have next to perfect control over their emotions. They do not feel love, hate, or any such emotion that is of value to us."
"That..."
Amaya's face turned grim. Nux, however, wasn't done yet.
"What they do have, however, is the thirst for power."
He smiled.
"Surprisingly, even though their love has faded away, their desire for power has not."
"Does this mean..."
Aeliana narrowed her eyes.
And Nux nodded.
"There is a strict balance of power maintained in Tenebris. Every Eternal—while they may appear to be each other's allies to Foreigners—wouldn't hesitate to get rid of each other if given a chance.
Rather, they have been looking for this chance all their lives."
"I thought they would be close to each other, like our Progenitors."
Skyla muttered.

"Our Progenitors have Lord Azriel above them. There is no thirst for power because Lord Azriel had all of it. Tenebris is different. Power is divided amongst the Four Eternals, and every single one of them wants more."
"So what are we going to do?"
Amaya questioned.
"We are going to give them what they want. Just like you said."
Nux grinned.
"We will give them power?"
Amaya raised her eyebrow.
"Yes. We will give them power to get rid of the other."
"And who will we be supporting?"
At that question, Nux's grin widened even further.
"All of them."

chapters.title: Chapter 1985 The Devil.
paragraphs: The instant Rivenar disappeared, Dainar, who was sitting on his throne and sensed his disappearance because of his connection with the Tenebris's Will, froze.

Soon, however, a grin appeared on his face as he sensed Sirecall being used again. He stood up, looking forward to meeting the being who was able to abduct his capable subordinates without leaving any trace at all.
He allowed his body to be teleported to wherever the Sirecall was activated, his body flickered as the Space energy surrounded him.
But then,
Flicker
His body disappeared and appeared right where he was.
He frowned.
The teleportation failed.
"What...?"
Once again, he tried sensing where the Sirecall was activated, but this time, the coordinates he got were changed, then they changed again, and again, then again and again.
The coordinates continued to change five times every single second, and Dainar, who was sensing them, narrowed his eyes. The coordinates couldn't be trusted; the Space Laws were being manipulated.
He finally understood who he was facing.
A being with Absolute Mastery over Space. In an instant, three names came to his mind. Only these three beings in the entire Universe were capable of doing something like this so effortlessly.
But...
None of them had any reason to go against him. Heck, if they so wished, they could directly deal with him, so why go after his subordinates?
Dainar's frown deepened.
Then suddenly,
Flicker
A silver spherical crystal appeared in his throne room, right in front of him.
He narrowed his eyes. Obviously, he knew what it was—a Call Artifact given to Quoril, another one of his subordinates who had been abducted.
Bzzz

Then, the Call Artifact started buzzing. It was being activated; someone was trying to contact him. A frosty look appeared on Dainar's face. He waved his hand, and the artifact started hovering in the air and flew toward him.
He picked up the call, and a foreign face he couldn't recognize appeared in front of him.

He had long black hair, long ears, black, curved horns, playful, almost arrogant purple eyes, wings on his back, and an extremely handsome face—too handsome, in fact. Even Dainar, whose beauty standards were different because the two of them were of entirely different races, could tell how good-looking this being was.
*Picture*
"Who are you?"
Dainar questioned directly.
The being grinned.
"The last time I appeared, they called me the Devil."
He replied. Then, he tilted his head with a frown and,
"Or was I the one who called myself that? I don't remember now; it has been a long time."
Dainar's mouth twitched. He finally realized who he was facing.
A crazy bastard.
"Why are you doing this?"
Not wanting to deal with him longer than required, Dainar decided to be direct.
"We have no enmity; I do not even know you. Why are you targeting my subordinates?"
"Do you really not know?"
The Devil grinned.
Dainar narrowed his eyes, and at his reaction, the Devil just chuckled.
"I thought you four were best of friends, you know? It seems I was wrong, very wrong."
"Is it those three bastards?"
Dainar questioned, not hiding his anger as he instantly pointed fingers at his fellow Progenitors.
The Devil just grinned, not saying anything.
"Why are you calling me?"
Dainar questioned.
Whoever this man was, he already had his subordinates. He had no reason to contact him if he was ordered to kill them, but since he had contacted him anyways...
Then there must be something he needed.
Negotiations might be possible.

"You are a smart man, Dainar. You know what you want, and you know how to get it. You should also know that you have no way to get your subordinates back no matter how desperately you try, at least, not until I want to give them back to you.
And women, of course. I am not really a fan of your people's fairer gender, so you can have them all.
The question is,
How much do you value your subordinates?"
At that question, Dainar just laughed.
"How much do you think I value them?"
"Not much, I presume."
The Devil laughed as well.
He had read all of Dainar's subordinates' memories; he knew quite a bit about this man now, so he could guess what he was trying to do.

By trying to show that he didn't value his subordinates, he was trying to gain power in the negotiation—a good tactic, especially considering that the Progenitor really didn't care about his subordinates very much.
Their loss would be... effortful.
Yes, effortful, since the other subordinates wouldn't be as efficient as them, as they wouldn't know the inner workings, and Dainar would need some time to train them.
Yes, that was it.
That was all the value his closest subordinates had for him.
Well, at least that was the case for this bunch of subordinates. The Devil, however, had different plans.
"Did you not wonder?"
Suddenly, the Devil questioned. Dainar frowned at those words, and the Devil continued.

"Those friends of yours know what sort of person you are, yet they still told me to abduct your subordinates. Did you really think they would do so without a plan? Are you not curious to know what their plan is?"
"You will tell me?"
Dainar raised his eyebrow, and the Devil just laughed.
"You have no way to stop it, so why not?"
"What is it? The plan."

"For the next ten thousand years, they have told me to abduct and kill all your close subordinates. This will not only get rid of your information network, but it will also give them a chance to push an agenda that you do not have the power to protect your men.

People under you will begin to live in fear, and then your friends will offer them a helping hand. Your people will switch sides, you will lose power in your own world, and once your allies in the other worlds find out about this, they will deem you to be incompetent, and you will lose them as well.
Your friends plan to take your subordinates, your people, and then your allies before they single you out and end you.
Quite efficient, even if I do say so myself.
I didn't know my powers could be used this way."

chapters.title: Chapter 1986 Deal with the Devil.
paragraphs: "Your friends plan to take your subordinates, your people, and then your allies before they single you out and end you.
Quite efficient, even if I do say so myself.
I didn't know my powers could be used this way."
The Devil laughed, clearly impressed by himself. Dainar, on the other hand, narrowed his eyes and,
"You think this would work?"
"What's stopping me?"
"Me."
"And how do you plan to do that?"
The Devil chuckled.
"Don't think you can stay hidden forever."
Dainar threatened, and at those words, the Devil's grin widened as he spread his arms and,
"I am right here, my friend. Use every power you have, call every ally who is willing to help you, and try to get to me.
I challenge you."
The Devil spoke, his purple eyes shining playfully.
"Go, go to your allies, tell them that you need their help to protect your own subordinates. I would like to see what their reaction would be.
Why don't you order your subordinate to contact them? Oh wait—"
The Devil then grabbed the head of an unconscious being and,
"—that subordinate is with me.
My bad, guess you would need to ask someone else~"

Seeing the man taunting him without a care in the world, Dainar clenched his fists in frustration. All this while, he had been trying—trying to sense the Sirecall's Coordinates, trying to get to this bastard and deal with him head-on, but...
"It doesn't work, does it?"
The Devil chuckled.
Then, suddenly, the Sirecall, the artifact Dainar had been trying to trace all this while, appeared in his hand.
"Quite an interesting thing, this one."
He muttered, staring at the artifact.

"It was constantly emitting Space Energy, trying to bring you here. I had to put quite some effort into making it stop, but even then, it is still trying to send you the coordinates so you can get here yourself.

Of course, I could destroy it to make it stop, but then where is the fun in that? Keep trying. I wish to see whether you would rather continue to resist pointlessly or act like the grown man you are and listen to my demands.
I assure you, it isn't something big. You see, I am a busy man. Even I do not wish to make someone's life miserable just because his friends do not like him."
The Devil chuckled. Soon, however, his expression changed as playful eyes turned frosty and,
"But I am also quite vindictive. Try to get in my way, and I will go out of my way to make sure you are destroyed.
You don't want to face that, trust me. It is not worth it, especially considering I am not asking for much."
"...What do you want?"
Dainar questioned.

He realized that even if he could find him and get to him, it would take time, and it was too much work. At the very least, he could listen to his demands. If it was something that wasn't too hard to accomplish, then negotiations could be done, saving him the pointless effort.
"The Temple of Time."
The Devil spoke, and the instant he heard those words, Dainar's expression changed.
"So you know about it."
The Devil grinned, noticing the change in Dainar's expression.

Honestly, even after absorbing Dainar's subordinates' memories, he hadn't found anything regarding the Temple of Time, so he was somewhat skeptical. Dainar's expression, however, made things somewhat easier.
"What do you wish to know?"
Dainar questioned.
"Everything you know about it. What it is, what it is used for, where it is—everything."
"And what do I get in return after I give you what you want?"
"Your subordinates back?"
The Devil tilted his head as if that was obvious, and Dainar just stared at him with a deadpan look on his face.
A staring contest started between the two until Dainar finally had enough of it and,
"You want me to give you information in exchange for the subordinates I do not even care about?"
Dainar's mouth twitched.
"It saves you quite a bit of effort, you know?
Do you truly wish to lose all your power just to hold onto the information you do not even care about anymore?"
"Do not care about anymore? Do you even know wha—"
"Stop pretending. Even your closest subordinates didn't know anything regarding the Temple of Time, and you clearly do not hide anything from them since you trust them quite a bit."
"Information regarding the Temple of Time isn't something I can trust my subordinates with."
Dainar answered directly.
And seeing that he wasn't giving in, the Devil just shrugged,
"Well, if you wish to play the long game, then..."
Just as he was about to end the call and contact the second leader to demand the same thing,
"Wait."
Dainar called out.
"What is it?"
"Attack them instead."
"Hmm?"
"Attack their subordinates instead. Make them lose power. Ally with me, and I'll tell you everything you need to know."
This time, the Devil was the one who stared at Dainar with a deadpan look on his face.
The second staring contest began, and this time, the Devil lost as he gave in.

"So you want me to help you, the losing side? How do you think that would even play out? Even if I abduct their subordinates, the moment you press forward and try to destroy their reputation, they will directly target and get rid of you.
I doubt you are strong enough to take on all of them. Siding with you is foolish. I might as well go to them and negotiate regarding the information.
I thought you, as the losing side, would be a better choice to get the information from, but it seems like I was wrong."
Once again, the Devil was about to cut the call, but then,
"...Then a favor."
Dainar called out.
"A promise that in the future, you will help me in anything as long as it doesn't endanger your life.
How about it?
Promise me that, and I will tell you everything there is to know about the Temple of Time."
"Now that's something that can be arranged.
You are finally learning how to make a Deal with the Devil."
The Devil grinned.

sentences.text: "Your friends plan to take your subordinates, your people, and then your allies before they single you out and end you.
Quite efficient, even if I do say so myself.
I didn't know my powers could be used this way."
The Devil laughed, clearly impressed by himself.
Dainar, on the other hand, narrowed his eyes and,
"You think this would work?"
"What's stopping me?"
"Me."
"And how do you plan to do that?"
The Devil chuckled.
"Don't think you can stay hidden forever."
Dainar threatened, and at those words, the Devil's grin widened as he spread his arms and,
"I am right here, my friend.
Use every power you have, call every ally who is willing to help you, and try to get to me.
I challenge you."
The Devil spoke, his purple eyes shining playfully.
"Go, go to your allies, tell them that you need their help to protect your own subordinates.
I would like to see what their reaction would be.
Why don't you order your subordinate to contact them?
Oh wait—"
The Devil then grabbed the head of an unconscious being and,
"—that subordinate is with me.
My bad, guess you would need to ask someone else~"
Seeing the man taunting him without a care in the world, Dainar clenched his fists in frustration.
All this while, he had been trying—trying to sense the Sirecall's Coordinates, trying to get to this bastard and deal with him head-on, but...
"It doesn't work, does it?"
The Devil chuckled.
Then, suddenly, the Sirecall, the artifact Dainar had been trying to trace all this while, appeared in his hand.
"Quite an interesting thing, this one."
He muttered, staring at the artifact.
"It was constantly emitting Space Energy, trying to bring you here.
I had to put quite some effort into making it stop, but even then, it is still trying to send you the coordinates so you can get here yourself.
Of course, I could destroy it to make it stop, but then where is the fun in that?
Keep trying.
I wish to see whether you would rather continue to resist pointlessly or act like the grown man you are and listen to my demands.
I assure you, it isn't something big.
You see, I am a busy man.
Even I do not wish to make someone's life miserable just because his friends do not like him."
The Devil chuckled.
Soon, however, his expression changed as playful eyes turned frosty and,
"But I am also quite vindictive.
Try to get in my way, and I will go out of my way to make sure you are destroyed.
You don't want to face that, trust me.
It is not worth it, especially considering I am not asking for much."
"...What do you want?"
Dainar questioned.
He realized that even if he could find him and get to him, it would take time, and it was too much work.
At the very least, he could listen to his demands.
If it was something that wasn't too hard to accomplish, then negotiations could be done, saving him the pointless effort.
"The Temple of Time."
The Devil spoke, and the instant he heard those words, Dainar's expression changed.
"So you know about it."
The Devil grinned, noticing the change in Dainar's expression.
Honestly, even after absorbing Dainar's subordinates' memories, he hadn't found anything regarding the Temple of Time, so he was somewhat skeptical.
Dainar's expression, however, made things somewhat easier.
"What do you wish to know?"
Dainar questioned.
"Everything you know about it.
What it is, what it is used for, where it is—everything."
"And what do I get in return after I give you what you want?"
"Your subordinates back?"
The Devil tilted his head as if that was obvious, and Dainar just stared at him with a deadpan look on his face.
A staring contest started between the two until Dainar finally had enough of it and,
"You want me to give you information in exchange for the subordinates I do not even care about?"
Dainar's mouth twitched.
"It saves you quite a bit of effort, you know?
Do you truly wish to lose all your power just to hold onto the information you do not even care about anymore?"
"Do not care about anymore?
Do you even know wha—"
"Stop pretending.
Even your closest subordinates didn't know anything regarding the Temple of Time, and you clearly do not hide anything from them since you trust them quite a bit."
"Information regarding the Temple of Time isn't something I can trust my subordinates with."
Dainar answered directly.
And seeing that he wasn't giving in, the Devil just shrugged,
"Well, if you wish to play the long game, then..."
Just as he was about to end the call and contact the second leader to demand the same thing,
"Wait."
Dainar called out.
"What is it?"
"Attack them instead."
"Hmm?"
"Attack their subordinates instead.
Make them lose power.
Ally with me, and I'll tell you everything you need to know."
This time, the Devil was the one who stared at Dainar with a deadpan look on his face.
The second staring contest began, and this time, the Devil lost as he gave in.
"So you want me to help you, the losing side?
How do you think that would even play out?
Even if I abduct their subordinates, the moment you press forward and try to destroy their reputation, they will directly target and get rid of you.

"...Then a favor."

Promise me that, and I will tell you everything there is to know about the Temple of Time."

You are finally learning how to make a Deal with the Devil."
The Devil grinned.

chapters.title: Chapter 1987 What is the Temple of Time?
paragraphs: "A promise that in the future, you will help me with anything I ask as long as it doesn't endanger your life.
Promise me that, and I will tell you everything there is to know about the Temple of Time."
"Now that's something that can be arranged.
You are finally learning how to make a deal with the Devil."
The Devil grinned.
"Good."
Dainar nodded as well.
"Then let's begin.
Temple of Time, tell me everything you know."
"Ask me what you want."
"That wasn't the deal."
Nux narrowed his eyes.
"I wouldn't know where to begin. I do not know what you know and what you do not. Ask, and I will begin from there."

Nux nodded in understanding. From what he knew about Dainar, it was very much possible that he was playing some tricks here, but Nux didn't care. As long as he got what he wanted, what Dainar did didn't matter.
The deal was made, so Nux began,
"What is the Temple of Time?"
He asked the most basic question. Dainar stared at him for a moment and then gave an answer.

"Time is a complicated power. In all of the Universe, the number of beings who have power over time is already fewer than normal, but even those who have power related to time do not have a complete understanding of it.

Some can control the speed of time, some can sense the flow of time, some can rewind time, some can manipulate the past and the future, some are able to break the flow of time, and finally, some can use time to manipulate Time Causality.
None of these beings, however, can do every single one of these things at the same time.
The Law of Time has always been incomplete."
"Isn't that the case with all the Laws?"
Nux questioned.
After all, even the Law of Death back in Umbrasol was always incomplete. Only he was able to complete it.
"It is."
Dainar nodded at his words.
"But the power of time is an exception. It is an extremely useful Law. Probably the strongest of all."
Nux didn't deny those words.

He could tell how having control over time would make one invincible. Take the Seer, for example. Even the Supreme Worlds, the strongest worlds in the Universe, who have absolute dominion over the Universe, cannot harm her.
The woman could do literally whatever she wanted, go wherever she wanted, and no one in this Universe, not even him, could sense her.
Heck, the woman even fooled Azriel.
Azriel mentioned that recording bit she pulled off. If something like that happened with Nux, he would have lost his mind.
He honestly pitied his father-in-law that day. To reveal all his power to capture someone, only to realize you were outdone—it was indeed frustrating.
"The Temple of Time is an ancient ground that beings from all over the Universe visit in order to form a Law of Time."
While Nux was thinking all this, Dainar revealed, and Nux raised his eyebrow.
"Then why do I not know about such an important place?"
He couldn't help but frown.
After all, Nux wasn't some world bumpkin who knew next to nothing about the Universe. He was probably one of the most knowledgeable beings in the entire Universe.

Even if he didn't know everything, he knew about most things. After all, he had the memory of one High-Level World and more than a few Middle, Low, and Lowest-Level Worlds. He highly doubted there were many people who had the same amount of information as him.
"It is said that if one clears all the trials of the Tower of Time, he will comprehend the Complete Law of Time."
Dainar answered.
It was a strange answer, something that made Nux frown. However, what attracted his attention were the words Dainar used.
"It is said...?"
Nux narrowed his eyes.
"No one has ever managed to clear all the trials."
Dainar revealed, and Nux's frown deepened.

"This is also the reason you probably do not know about the Temple of Time. It was well-known quite a long time ago. Many people tried their luck and took the trials, but they only returned with a weak law that destroyed their future.

It is said that even the Supreme World of Eternity once took over the place for five hundred thousand years, trying to study its structure and see if it was even possible to learn the Complete Law of Time. They sent countless Protectors to try and form a strong Law, but they all returned with Laws much weaker than they would have normally comprehended. Eventually, even the Supreme World of Eternity gave up and considered the Temple to be a waste of time and potential.

They abandoned the Temple alone. However, since even the world with the greatest knowledge abandoned the place, the Temple continued to wither away. Of course, in their thirst for power, many still tried their luck, but every single being, without any exception, returned without success.
Millions of years later, beings all over the Universe finally started believing the World of Eternity's words. The Temple was abandoned by everyone, and it lost its popularity.

Of course, this was millions, if not billions, of years ago, so most worlds, even the High-Level Worlds, do not know about the Temple now. They hear the rumours and treat it like some myth, just like we once did."
"Then... what about now?"
Nux questioned.
"Why do you know about all this now?"
"We looked into it."
"What?"
Nux tilted his head.

"One of Tenebris's closest allies was infatuated by the power of time. When our worlds heard about this Temple of Time, while he thought it to be a myth, they were different. Their Progenitor wanted to know if this place actually existed."
"How did they find out?"
"They went to the most assured source of information."
Nux's expression changed when he heard those words.
"Eternity..."
"Yes, they made a deal with the Supreme World of Eternity."
Dainar nodded.

chapters.title: Chapter 1988 He was different.
paragraphs: "They went to the most assured source of information."
Nux's expression changed when he heard those words.
"Eternity..."
"Yes, they made a deal with the Supreme World of Eternity."
Dainar nodded. He wasn't surprised that Nux knew the answer; after all, everyone in this Universe knew what the most assured source of information was.

If there was anything, literally anything you wished to know, you went to the Supreme World of Eternity. It didn't matter what it was—information about an ancient relic, about a world that was destroyed millions of years ago, or even information about your girlfriend's bathing habits.
Eternity would know it all.
Just that...
The price of getting that information was often not very cheap.
"We and the Progenitors of Orynthar exchanged five High-Level Relics in order to get the information. So keep this in mind,
what I am giving you is not cheap in any way.

I can confidently say that other than the Supreme Worlds and we four Progenitors of Tenebris, almost no one else knows about the Temple of Time. And those who do only think of it as a myth and don't bother looking into it.
I am actually surprised you even came to me to get this information, almost as if you knew exactly where to go to get what you need."
"I have a talent in that regard. If I want something, I take it, one way or the other."
Nux grinned.
"That is good."
Dainar nodded.
"The more resourceful you are, the better it is for me."
He grinned.
Nux smiled as well before he asked another question.
"Why was Orynthar so obsessed with the Temple of Time?"
Dainar frowned at that question.
"Why are you? Or why is anyone else?
Power."
The answer was simple.
"And did the two worlds attain that power?"
Nux questioned, and Dainar just laughed.
"Even the Supreme World of Eternity failed. You think we would have succeeded?"
"So you..."
"We failed.

The result was just as the Supreme World of Eternity mentioned. We sent our Protectors, and they returned with a Law far weaker than they would have normally formed. Most of them decided to kill themselves."
"What sort of Laws did they form? Were they related to time?"

"They were. But they were extremely weak. Most of them couldn't even clear one Trial, let alone all, so the Laws they formed were merely some little temporal manipulation with severe restrictions. The best we got was the ability to stop the flow of time for a minute. It was a terrible failure."
Dainar still felt his heart bleed when he recalled the cost they paid to learn about that damned place.
"Why only send Protectors? Why not stronger beings?"
Nux questioned, curious.
"And do what? The place was built to form a Law. How are beings above the Sovereign Stage supposed to form a Law?"
"Why not try and understand the Temple itself?"
"It is just a place with some trials. What is there to understand?"
Nux didn't know what to say.
How this man became the leader of a High-Level World, he had no clue.
"Can beings stronger than Protectors enter the place?"
"They probably can. One of the Progenitors of Orynthar walked in."
"And what did he say?"
"What else? As I said, it was useless. That place is a sham!"
Dainar lost his composure.
"If that place is a sham, then am I not making a bad deal here? Why would I promise you a favour in exchange for a sham?"
"Because you will still want to go there."
Dainar's answer was simple.
"Why is that?"
Nux narrowed his eyes. He felt like he was missing something.
"Because you think you are different from us."
Dainar grinned.
"Even we felt the same.

So what if the Supreme World of Eternity failed? It is very much possible that the most knowledgeable world in the entire Universe missed something—something that we might not. And who knows? All this talk about the place being useless might be a trick by the Supreme World of Eternity so they could prevent us from going there and getting stronger.
All those foolish thoughts pushed us, and they will push you as well.
What we, the Supreme World of Eternity, and all those worlds millions of years ago couldn't do, you would believe that you will be able to do it,
So you will go."
Nux turned silent.
This... actually made sense.
After all, he was different from these plebs.
He would obviously be able to clear all the Tower Trials and form the Complete Law of Time. There was no doubt about that.
Seeing his expression, Dainar just grinned, knowing exactly what he was thinking. After all, he had the same line of thought once.
"So? What else do you wish to know?"
He questioned.
"The coordinates. Where is the Temple of Time?"
"5823232.423287334. Universal Coordinates."
Nux noted it down as Dainar continued.
"It is currently under the control of a High-Level World named Timeguard."
"I have never heard about this world."
Nux frowned.

"Well, if you had, you would have known about the Temple of Time. It is a desolate world devoid of life. There are only about 50 beings living there. Most of them have given their entire lives trying to peek into the secrets of the Temple of Time."
Dainar then looked into Nux's eyes and—
"Just the people you wanted. Ones who are trying to comprehend the Temple itself. They have been doing this their entire life, and of course, they are failing quite miserably."
"...How strong are they?"
Nux questioned directly.
If they weren't as strong, then maybe he could read their memories and learn about them and the Temple itself, but...
"The strongest amongst them is a Peak Eternal, one of the strongest beings in the Universe. His four direct subordinates are all Eternals. The rest are Transcendents."
Nux turned silent, quickly abandoning his initial thoughts.
It seemed like he needed to act like a good boy here.
He chuckled at that thought. Then suddenly, a crystal ball appeared right in front of Dainar. Dainar frowned, and then—
"Whenever you wish to call in your favour, activate that artifact and contact me. If I am not too busy, I will pick up."
"Hey! There was no deal about being bus—"
"There was no deal about the Temple being a sham either."
Nux chuckled as he then cut the call.
Dainar's mouth twitched in annoyance. He, however, just shook his head and picked up the artifact Nux gave him.
On the other side, Nux, who was hovering in outer space, grabbed another being he had just kidnapped—an action that made Felberta frown.
"What are you doing?"
She questioned.
"Confirming what we found."

Just like that, Nux contacted another Tenebris Progenitor, and only after he confirmed the details regarding the Temple of Time with all four Progenitors did he finally decide to make a move and teleport in front of Timeguard.
