On the other side, Nux, who was hovering in outer space, grabbed another being he had just kidnapped—an action that made Felberta frown.
"What are you doing?"
She questioned.
"Confirming what we found."

Just like that, Nux contacted another Tenebris Progenitor, and only after he confirmed the details regarding the Temple of Time with all four Progenitors did he finally decide to make a move and teleport in front of Timeguard.

chapters.title: Chapter 1989 When is this going to happen?
paragraphs: A being sitting cross-legged hovered in the air. He had purple skin, long ears resembling an imp, a bald head, and a white mark on his head. He wore monk-like clothes and continued to meditate without a single change in his expression.

He was inside a simple, regular-sized room, with normal beige walls, a mat placed on the floor instead of a bed, and a small window. If one didn't know him, they would think he was a villager who had nothing to show for himself and was living a meagre life.
Unless, of course, they came close to him and sensed his cultivation level.
He was an Eternal, and not just any Eternal—he was one of the strongest Eternals in the Universe.
He was also one of the oldest Eternals, one of the beings who had lived through the time when there were Five Supreme Worlds instead of Four.
Yes, he was THAT old. Most of his peers had forced themselves to sleep or had simply entered the reincarnation cycle since they couldn't stand immortality any longer, but he... he held on.
He was knowledgeable and strong enough to take on almost any Eternal-level being who stood against him, yet...
Almost no one in this entire Universe knew about him.
And how would they?
Ever since he was a Protector, he had confined himself in Timeguard and had never left the place again.
Yes, he was also one of those beings who tried their luck comprehending time. Unlike most, however, he didn't fail.
Although he wasn't able to form a Complete Law of Time, he was able to understand and master the Temporal Flow.

Yes, he was the holder of the Law of Absolute Time Manipulation, one of the strongest Time Laws. He could manipulate the speed of time to any degree he desired, around any area he desired—a power that would pretty much make him invincible if he ever used it for combat.
All he had to do was slow the time around his enemies. Once the enemy was frozen, he had thousands of ways to get rid of them. It was never even a fair battle since his Law was an Absolute.
Yes, that was how strong this being was.
"Master Tenzin!"
While the being, Tenzin, was cultivating, a woman barged into his room, panicked. It was completely opposite of the calm and serene aura Tenzin had created around himself.

Tenzin opened his eyes and stared at the woman who had walked in. The woman had pale white skin and a beautiful figure—even the loose monk clothing couldn't hide her curves. She had no hair, just like Tenzin, and she covered her eyes with a blindfold.
The blindfold, however, didn't seem to hinder her vision since she moved around just fine, even avoiding Tenzin's mat where he rested as she rushed toward him.
"Calm down, Vashti."
Tenzin called out, his voice as calm as always.
His words, however, seemed to have no effect on Vashti. Rather, she grabbed Tenzin's arm and—
"Someone is going to read my memories!"
"What...?"
Tenzin's expression changed.
"I sensed it a few minutes ago. I wasn't killed, neither was I hurt. My mind, however, had a blank, and once Lord Solus examined me, he realized that my memories were read."
"Who did it?"
Tenzin narrowed his eyes.
"I do not know!"
Vashti answered.
"What do you mean?"
Tenzin couldn't understand.
"Did you not see it?"

"I did not! I tried doing everything. I did not see anything. I only know I was suddenly teleported to Outer Space. I tried returning but couldn't. A force I couldn't comprehend nor see neutralized me, and after a few hours, I was sent back."
"You didn't... see anyone?"
"I did not!"
Vashti shook her head, unable to comprehend what was happening to her.
"How were you neutralized then?"
"I do not know; I just couldn't move!"
"Was it the Power of Confinement?"
"It was similar, but I didn't sense anything. It was some invisible force that couldn't be sensed. To me, it looked like I stopped moving without any apparent reason!"
"You just stopped moving...?"
Tenzin's frown deepened. He had spent almost all his life trying to unravel the mystery behind the Temple of Time. He was used to dealing with the unknown, so almost nothing ever surprised him.
But this... this was different.
Vashti was his greatest student, someone with a potential as strong as his, if not stronger.
The Law of Absolute Projection.
It was a Law that allowed her to create future and past projections of others and herself. She could recreate events that happened in the past and the events that would happen in the future.

Of course, recreating events in the future was much more complicated since even the slightest change could create thousands of timelines, so the farther into the future one tries to see, the less accurate it becomes.
Then there was also the problem of losing herself in one of those future timelines or overloading her brain with all the information, so she had to be extremely careful.
However, this didn't mean her Law was weak. In fact, it was much stronger.
Vashti's Law gave her an unbelievable precognition ability. In her still life, where all she did was meditate, the moment something out of the ordinary happened, she was able to sense it.

Even when Orynthar and Tenebris were about to visit, she was the first one to sense their arrival and inform them all. She told them exactly who was coming, what they were coming for, and when they would leave.
Honestly, if she wasn't hell-bent on spending most of her time studying the Temple of Time, she would have long broken through the Eternal Stage.
Right now, however, none of that mattered.
According to Vashti, someone would read her memory in the future—someone she couldn't see or sense. This didn't make sense.
Was it really possible to read someone's memory without leaving any trace whatsoever?
There were countless questions in Tenzin's head. For now, however, protecting his disciple was much more important.
"When is this going to happen?"
"In 2 hours."

chapters.title: Chapter 1990 I believe you can stop this, Master Tenzin.
paragraphs: "When is this going to happen?"
"In 2 hours."
Tenzin couldn't understand.
"Someone is going to capture you and read your memories in just 2 hours, and you are telling this to me now?"
"I didn't know it was going to happen before this."
"...what?"
Tenzin's frown deepened even further. This entire conversation was getting over his head.
With Vashti's current powers, she should be able to sense something like this years ago. She predicted Tenebris and Orynthar's arrival a decade before it happened.
Then how is...
"These events started unfolding a few minutes ago," Vashti answered.
"That shouldn't be possible. No event unfolds 2 hours before it actually happens. Everything is already set in stone. It depends on our ability as to how efficiently we can predict it."
This was an absolute truth.
Vashti knew this as well.

Even when the Tenebris and Orynthar came to them, it didn't just happen because one day, the Orynthar Progenitors became interested in the Power of Time and heard the rumour regarding the Temple of Time.

It was set in stone from the very beginning. The Orynthar Progenitors were meant to be interested in the Power of Time because of certain events in their lives. They were meant to hear about the Temple of Time. They were meant to go to Tenebris. The two worlds were meant to go to the Supreme World of Eternity, and so on...
Of course, Vashti didn't know it all from the start. She only learned about all this when these events happened and the two worlds were about to make a deal with the Supreme World of Eternity.
However, the instant Vashti learned about this event, it was very much possible to trace back those events in the past with much more certainty.
The current set of events should be the same as well. Vashti wouldn't be abducted just because someone thought about it 2 hours ago.
A set of events must have happened that led to this. Events Vashti should be able to trace back...
But...
"This is... different," Vashti spoke up.
"I tried tracing back, but...
I didn't see anything."
"What...?"
"Currently, Lord Dainar from Tenebris is telling someone about the Temple of Time. I suspect whoever that being is, he is the one coming for me."
"Then see who this being is."
"I cannot."
"Why?"
"Lord Dainar is using a Call Artifact to converse, and I cannot connect any time strings to the other side of the call.
It is as if whatever Lord Dainar is doing is all an act, which I would have believed if I hadn't verified the matter of his conversation."
"What is it?" Tenzin questioned.

"Whoever this being is, he has abducted Lord Dainar's subordinates, which is indeed true. When I looked into the abducted subordinates, I found them hovering in outer space. Their state was similar to mine."
"So whoever this being is, he is threatening Dainar using his subordinates?"
"Lord Dainar proposed a deal that was accepted. Lord Dainar was promised a favour in exchange for the information regarding the Temple of Time."
Vashti answered, and Tenzin turned silent.
This was... odd.
To think someone like Dainar would agree to make a deal with someone just because of his subordinates... this wasn't the kind of man he was.
Something didn't add up here.
For now, however, Tenzin didn't have the time to think about Dainar. If Vashti had seen it, it meant that whoever that being was, he was coming.
But...
"This being seems to be interested in the Tower of Time. He must have read your memories because he wishes to know more about the Tower."
"That could be the case."
Vashti nodded.
"Have you tried changing your course of action?" Tenzin questioned.
"I have. Nothing I do changes the future events, except..."
"Except?"
"Except when I enter the Temple of Time."
"Well..."
Tenzin shook his head. Vashti nodded as well.

That was normal. The Temple of Time protects the Trial Takers from any outside influence, no matter how strong. Let alone whoever this being was—even the Supreme Worlds wouldn't be able to harm Vashti if she was inside the Temple.
The problem, however, was that...
"In that possibility, the instant I come out of the Tower, I am captured. So unless I stay inside the Tower for the rest of my life..."
Tenzin shook his head.
One couldn't stay inside the Temple of Time for too long. They would simply lose their mind. Even he, with all the knowledge and power he had, couldn't stay inside for more than five hundred years.
"So it is not under your control, huh..."
Tenzin sighed.
"This is why I came to you."
"Has being around me altered the future?" Tenzin questioned.
"It has not."
Vashti answered, making Tenzin frown. Vashti, however, wasn't done yet.
"But I believe you can stop this, Master Tenzin."
"How?"

"Whoever this being is, he is targeting Transcendents of weaker-level beings. He wanted information—information that Lord Dainar had. He has the ability to read minds, yet he didn't read Lord Dainar's mind and made a deal instead.
There is a possibility that he is avoiding direct confrontation with Eternal Level Beings."
"Then why hasn't being around me altered your future?"
"That being has power over space. To him, it shouldn't matter where I am since he could move me wherever he wishes to. But if we somehow seal the Space energy..."
Vashti didn't have to complete her words.

Tenzin closed his eyes and raised his hand. In an instant, his surroundings changed. His simple room twisted—walls stretched and contracted as if breathing. The wooden table aged centuries in a blink, then reversed, returning to its freshly carved state. Dust hung midair, frozen, while a phantom clock appeared in the sky as its hands spun wildly, unable to settle on a moment.
Yes, it was his Domain.
However, as a Domain of an Eternal, it didn't just give him power over time—it made him Absolute.
"Space."
He muttered, and in an instant, the very concept of space vanished within his domain.
Once again, he turned towards his disciple.
Vashti stayed silent for a moment, and then, she nodded.
"It worked."
Yes, the woman was now safe.

chapters.title: Chapter 1991 My people call me Tenzin.
paragraphs: After talking to all 4 Leaders of Tenebris, Nux let out a sigh.
"...What are you going to do now?"
Felberta questioned as she appeared next to him.
"They aren't lying, that we can be sure about."
Astaria commented.
"But their words do not match."
Rune muttered.
"It is as if they remember an entirely different Temple of Time."
Thyra spoke up as well.
"The biggest issue is that none of the Trial Takers are alive, so we only have 4 testimonies."
Riona added, and the rest of the women groaned.

Nux had a conversation with all of Tenebris's Leaders and convinced them to give him the information regarding the place. While the coordinates of the place and basic introduction were the same, when he asked what was inside in order to prepare, their answers were vague.

The thing was, the Temple of Time wasn't an eventful conquest for the Tenebris leaders. If anything, it was shameful. And since they themselves didn't experience it and only sent Protector Level Beings—who all returned with disappointing results—the Leaders didn't even bother listening to the details other than some formal reports.
What's even stranger was that all four Leaders had almost entirely different descriptions of what was inside. This made things even more confusing.
"It could be that the Temple changes according to the person who enters."
Aisha spoke up.
The rest of the women nodded as they turned towards Nux. Nux nodded back. He had considered this option, and it made sense. Just that...

The information he had was still too vague. He had convinced himself not to, but it seemed like he had to abduct a Transcendent staying in Timeguard and read his memories to know more about the place.
Those people had spent all their lives trying to learn about the Temple; they should have answers to his questions.
With that thought in his mind, Nux nodded at his wives. They nodded back, agreeing with his thoughts, as he then teleported everyone to the dimensions he was given.

Nux and his wives then appeared right in front of a world that looked nothing like the High-Level World they had seen all this while. The size of this world was smaller than even the Lowest Level Worlds. Honestly, looking at this world, Nux felt curious.
For a moment, he wanted to devour it to know more about it, but he then controlled his desires and focused on the matter in front of him.
He glanced at his wives and, as if knowing what he was thinking, the wives' bodies were engulfed by their shadows, everyone returning to his Universe.

Once again, Nux's gaze returned to the world in front of him. He stepped forward and disappeared, appearing right inside the world. He was still using Vulpiana's Law to hide himself, and while he was worried about being caught this time since people here could very much sense different Timelines, he wasn't planning on staying here for long.
He just needed to abduct one Transcendent and get what he wanted.
With that thought in his mind, he closed his eyes and expanded his senses.
And the moment he did,
"What the..."
He frowned.
All 53 beings of this world were standing together with an Eternal Level Being, who, for some odd reason, had activated his Domain.
A Domain whose space could not be breached, and teleporting anything inside it or from it was impossible.
"Who in their right mind keeps a Domain active all the time?"
Nux frowned in confusion.
Since he had time on his hands, he wanted to wait it out. After all, they couldn't just spend their entire life in a Domain, now could they? Their energy would run out eventually, no?
It wouldn't.
There were five Eternals in Tenebris.
If one created a Domain, the other four could continue to cultivate and regenerate their energy, making it so that the group never ran out of energy.
Now were they crazy enough to pull this off?
Nux highly doubted it, but then,
'Hmm?'
He noticed something.
When he expanded his senses, he had ignored this, but...
Bzzzz
Thousands of Call Artifacts that were randomly placed on the ground all over the world buzzed at the same time. Clearly, this was done on purpose.

Nux narrowed his eyes. He teleported outside Timeguard—far from it, actually—so the Eternals there could not chase him. Then, he sealed the space around him, making it impossible to teleport next to him, and activated the buzzing artifact. A screen appeared in front of him, showing a purple, goblin-like being who wore a monk's dress.
'A goblin monk was the last thing I was expecting...'
He muttered inwardly, staring at the being with a deadpan look on his face.
"So you are the Devil."
The Goblin Monk spoke.
Nux raised his eyebrow, surprised. The Goblin Monk smiled lightly.
"My people call me Tenzin."
He introduced himself politely.
"People call me Devil."
Nux answered, still keeping the persona.
Tenzin nodded as if he already knew that.
"I was hoping we could have a conversation, Devil."

He spoke. Once again, his tone was extremely polite. If Nux hadn't personally sensed his cultivation to be at the very Peak of the Eternal Stage, he would have thought he was some neighbourhood old man who always had a smile on his face.
"I... I was hoping so as well."
He answered, which made Tenzin chuckle.
"To call reading my disciple's memories a conversation. Your ways are indeed quite devilish, your name suits you."
Nux raised his eyebrow.

"Do not be too surprised, Devil. The disciple you were trying to abduct is the greatest achievement of my life. She has spent all her life studying time and has reached a certain level of mastery. She was able to sense that you were coming for her."

Tenzin answered with a smile, almost as if he didn't care that the man in front of him would have literally abducted his disciple and read her memories if he hadn't protected her. Heck, he even showed his disciple on the screen,
'Wait, she is...'
Nux raised his eyebrow.
This woman...
She looked familiar...
As if he had seen her before.

What's even stranger was that all four Leaders had almost entirely different descriptions of what was inside.
This made things even more confusing.
"It could be that the Temple changes according to the person who enters."
Aisha spoke up.
The rest of the women nodded as they turned towards Nux.
Nux nodded back.
He had considered this option, and it made sense.
Just that...
The information he had was still too vague.
He had convinced himself not to, but it seemed like he had to abduct a Transcendent staying in Timeguard and read his memories to know more about the place.
Those people had spent all their lives trying to learn about the Temple; they should have answers to his questions.
With that thought in his mind, Nux nodded at his wives.
They nodded back, agreeing with his thoughts, as he then teleported everyone to the dimensions he was given.
Nux and his wives then appeared right in front of a world that looked nothing like the High-Level World they had seen all this while.
The size of this world was smaller than even the Lowest Level Worlds.
Honestly, looking at this world, Nux felt curious.
For a moment, he wanted to devour it to know more about it, but he then controlled his desires and focused on the matter in front of him.
He glanced at his wives and, as if knowing what he was thinking, the wives' bodies were engulfed by their shadows, everyone returning to his Universe.
Once again, Nux's gaze returned to the world in front of him.
He stepped forward and disappeared, appearing right inside the world.

He was still using Vulpiana's Law to hide himself, and while he was worried about being caught this time since people here could very much sense different Timelines, he wasn't planning on staying here for long.
He just needed to abduct one Transcendent and get what he wanted.
With that thought in his mind, he closed his eyes and expanded his senses.
And the moment he did,
"What the..."
He frowned.
All 53 beings of this world were standing together with an Eternal Level Being, who, for some odd reason, had activated his Domain.
A Domain whose space could not be breached, and teleporting anything inside it or from it was impossible.
"Who in their right mind keeps a Domain active all the time?"
Nux frowned in confusion.
Since he had time on his hands, he wanted to wait it out.
After all, they couldn't just spend their entire life in a Domain, now could they?
Their energy would run out eventually, no?
It wouldn't.
There were five Eternals in Tenebris.
If one created a Domain, the other four could continue to cultivate and regenerate their energy, making it so that the group never ran out of energy.
Now were they crazy enough to pull this off?
Nux highly doubted it, but then,
'Hmm?'
He noticed something.
When he expanded his senses, he had ignored this, but...
Bzzzz
Thousands of Call Artifacts that were randomly placed on the ground all over the world buzzed at the same time.
Clearly, this was done on purpose.
Nux narrowed his eyes.
He teleported outside Timeguard—far from it, actually—so the Eternals there could not chase him.
Then, he sealed the space around him, making it impossible to teleport next to him, and activated the buzzing artifact.
A screen appeared in front of him, showing a purple, goblin-like being who wore a monk's dress.
'A goblin monk was the last thing I was expecting...'
He muttered inwardly, staring at the being with a deadpan look on his face.
"So you are the Devil."
The Goblin Monk spoke.
Nux raised his eyebrow, surprised.
The Goblin Monk smiled lightly.
"My people call me Tenzin."
He introduced himself politely.
"People call me Devil."
Nux answered, still keeping the persona.
Tenzin nodded as if he already knew that.
"I was hoping we could have a conversation, Devil."
He spoke.
Once again, his tone was extremely polite.
If Nux hadn't personally sensed his cultivation to be at the very Peak of the Eternal Stage, he would have thought he was some neighbourhood old man who always had a smile on his face.
I was hoping so as well."
He answered, which made Tenzin chuckle.
"To call reading my disciple's memories a conversation.
Your ways are indeed quite devilish, your name suits you."
Nux raised his eyebrow.
"Do not be too surprised, Devil.
The disciple you were trying to abduct is the greatest achievement of my life.
She has spent all her life studying time and has reached a certain level of mastery.
She was able to sense that you were coming for her."
Tenzin answered with a smile, almost as if he didn't care that the man in front of him would have literally abducted his disciple and read her memories if he hadn't protected her.
Heck, he even showed his disciple on the screen,
'Wait, she is...'
Nux raised his eyebrow.
This woman...
She looked familiar...
As if he had seen her before.

chapters.title: Chapter 1992 Vashti
paragraphs: 'Wait, she is...'

Nux raised his eyebrow as he stared at the woman on the screen. She had no hair, but that didn't take her beauty away. Her face was nothing short of perfect. She had beautiful, clear skin, and pink, soft lips. Her eyes were covered with a blindfold.
She wore extremely loose robes, almost as if she was trying to hide her sinful body, but the robes weren't doing a very good job.
The moment Nux's eyes fell on her, he frowned.
This woman...
She looked familiar, as if he had seen her before.
"Devil."

The woman spoke up. Her voice seemed familiar as well; Nux just couldn't seem to recall where he had heard it. Which was strange in its own way, considering that this man had memories of literal worlds in his head, and he remembered it all.
For now, however, Nux decided to continue the conversation and nodded at the woman. Once again, the screen shifted back to Tenzin and the monk continued,
"Of course, considering how your focus shifted to the rest of my disciples after I brought Vashti under my protection, it is clear that you aren't after her but something else instead."
Nux narrowed his eyes, but Tenzin didn't stop.
"So let us have a direct conversation and solve the matter, Devil.
What is it that you want?"
"I wish to know more about the Temple of Time."
Nux answered.
Although reading their memories was much more convenient since he wouldn't have to worry about them lying, for now, he didn't have another choice.
They already had a counter against him; he was helpless.
"What do you wish to know?"
"About the Trials. I tried asking others, but their answers were vague."
"That is expected."
Tenzin nodded.
"Tenebris Leaders weren't satisfied with the results. They thought of the Temple to be a sham, just like they were told, and didn't bother investing time in keeping clear records."
The Monk spoke and Nux nodded; that was exactly what happened.
"This is why I came to you."
"It is a difficult question to answer."
Tenzin began.
"The Temple is... one of the few mysteries of the Universe that even the Supreme Worlds of Eternity failed to comprehend.
It is an Ancient Ground, a place that is believed to be older than even the Supreme Worlds. It is said that the Temple existed even before our Universe did, but there are no records proving that.
The Trials inside the Temple change with each participant. The Tower assesses the trial takers and creates custom trials for them, so even if I wish to tell you, I cannot.

I can, however, give you the records of the previous Trial Takers and the trials they faced. Of course, almost every one of them failed at their first trial, while only the exceptional few managed to clear the first and enter the second trial. The trials they took still varied from person to person, but they still had some level of similarities.
I believe going through those records will give you the answers you are looking for."
Tenzin spoke. Once again, Nux couldn't help but notice how polite this man was. It was an extremely strange experience for a brute like him.
He also noticed another thing that made him raise his eyebrow.
"So some people did manage to clear the first trial?"
"Yes, by Time's grace, I was one of them."
Tenzin smiled.
"What about the Second Trial? Did anyone manage to clear it?"
"Only one being. Surprisingly, that being also managed to clear the third and fourth trials, only failing the fifth."
Tenzin answered, and although his face didn't show much of an expression, his tone couldn't hide his pride.
"Who is that?"
Nux couldn't help but question, and this time, a big smile appeared on Tenzin's face.
"Vashti."
Nux's expression changed as once again, Tenzin pulled his disciple close to him with a proud look on his face. Vashti, on the other hand, seemed a little embarrassed by being in the spotlight.
"And how many trials are there?"
"Vashti says there are six."
"Hmm?"
Nux frowned at those words.

"You learn more things about the Tower as you continue to clear the Trials. This is why we have been trying to clear the Trials even when we know doing so wouldn't change anything since we have already formed our Laws."
Soon, however, a self-deprecating smile appeared on Tenzin's face as he shook his head,
"Not that it matters, since all of us have failed to clear the second trial even after devoting all our lives to it.
I always wonder how Vashti manages to clear trial after trial as she progresses."
Tenzin spoke, and Nux couldn't help but feel impressed.
His eyes once again fell on the woman, and once again, the same thought appeared in his mind.
This woman...
She was too familiar.
He could swear he had seen her somewhere before.
'Will she think I am flirting with her if I say it out loud?'
Nux wondered in his head.
Seeing that the Devil was staring at his disciple, Tenzin smiled and continued,

"Do you want me to give you the records I mentioned? Those records also have detailed reports of every time Vashti entered the Temple, and since those reports were written by Vashti herself, they are quite well organized."
"Please."
Nux nodded.

It was an offer he couldn't reject. Honestly, he found it strange. He came here with the intention to abduct this man's disciple and read their memories, yet he is still trying to help him instead of bashing him away.
'Are the monks that good...?'
He couldn't help but wonder in his head.
He wasn't much of a spiritual guy, not in this life, nor in his past one, so he didn't know much.
Not to mention, because these people were so reclusive, none of the worlds or people whose memories he read had any information regarding them.
Nux was completely new to this.
And as if knowing what he was thinking, Tenzin continued,
"The Temple of Time is not ours. We consider it to be a gift from the Universe to its children. It belongs to us all, so we never gatekeep from others.
You came here because you were curious about it, and I gave you everything you need. I hope this solves the matter between us peacefully.
If not...
I will not hesitate to go to the Supreme Worlds and report your existence to them, Anomaly."
*Tenzin* *Vashti*

chapters.title: Chapter 1993 If something happens, I will kill myself.
paragraphs: "I will not hesitate to go to the Supreme Worlds and report your existence to them, Anomaly."
Tenzin spoke as he looked right into Nux's eyes.
Nux's expression faltered ever so slightly, something that Tenzin didn't fail to catch as he smiled lightly.

"The time you chose to appear isn't very convenient. All Four Supreme Worlds and their direct subordinates are looking for you. The Universe has been on edge for a while now—we feel its effect even here, in the corner of the Universe no one bothers to visit.
It isn't exactly difficult to put two and two together, especially considering how mysterious your existence is."

Nux stayed silent. For some reason, he didn't feel alarmed by Tenzin. Not only could he run away and hide in his Universe for an indefinite amount of time, Nux felt like Tenzin himself didn't wish to act on it.
And he was correct.

"Do not worry. As I said, unless you go back on your word and harm one of my disciples, I will not do anything. My disciples and I have given ourselves to the Study of Time. We have never involved ourselves in Universal Struggles, and we do not wish to become a part of it now.
My only wish is that once you get what you want, you leave this place without causing any harm."
"How do I know you wouldn't encircle me the moment I get inside the Temple of Time?"
Nux questioned directly.
"Once you are inside the Temple, even the Supreme Worlds wouldn't be able to harm you. The Temple protects the Trial Takers."
"What about after the Trial ends? I cannot keep hiding in the Temple for the rest of my life."
"I knew you were coming, Anomaly. Quite a long time ago. If I wanted, I could have contacted the Supreme Worlds and had you captured.
You didn't think hiding in another Timeline would protect you from them, did you?"
Nux turned silent.
"As I said, my disciples and I do not wish to be involved in the Universal Power Struggle. Enter the Trial grounds or send your men, disciples, or anyone you wish. Once you are done, leave.
That is all I ask, and in return, I will give you all the information you desire."
Tenzin spoke calmly, even taking out the records he mentioned.
"Basic information regarding the Temple of Time, and those records—keep them out of your domain."

Nux spoke cautiously. Tenzin stored all the documents in a storage device and did as he was told. Nux teleported the artifact into his hands. He nodded as he checked its contents, then bowed his head respectfully.
"Thank you for your help, Lord Tenzin."
Tenzin nodded at those words.

The call ended. Nux read all the documents Tenzin had sent him. It didn't take him a long time to store all the information. He did, however, take his time sorting through the information, especially when he read about Vashti and how she cleared the Trials every time she broke through a major phase.
She cleared the First Trial when she was a Protector and formed the Law of Absolute Projection.
Once she broke through to the Sovereign Stage, she cleared the Second Trial.
Breaking through the Primordial Stage allowed her to clear the Third Trial, and the Fourth Trial when she became a Transcendent.
'Following this pattern, she would clear all the Trials if she were to become an Infinity.'
Nux couldn't help but think of this absurd thought.
The number of Infinities in this world was extremely limited. With Azriel gone, there were probably only four of them now, each leading a Supreme World.
No other being, in billions of years, had reached this level, but...
No one has ever cleared four Temple of Time Trials either. Rather, this was an even rarer achievement. There had still been a few Infinities in the Universe, but someone like Vashti was unique.
A never-before-seen genius.
Thinking that someone like her could reach Infinity and clear all the Trials wasn't as absurd as one would think.
"She... sure is interesting."
Amaya, who knew what Nux was thinking, narrowed her eyes.
"Indeed, and she indeed feels quite familiar."
Aeliana nodded as well. Obviously, she didn't mean those words. With how her crimson eyes were glaring at Nux, he knew exactly what she meant.
Nux smiled wryly. He turned toward the two Yanderes who had decided to team up for some reason and,
"Tell me you do not think she looks familiar."
"She does not."
"She does not."
Both women answered at the same time, their tone deadpan yet decisive.
Nux couldn't say anything, not when he was being subjected to that gaze.
It looked... beautiful.
He wanted nothing more than to jump on these two and never let them go, but—
"You should go take the Trial. I still do not trust those monks."
Riona spoke up with a slight frown on her face.
Everything felt a little too simple. They got what they desired and even more, a little too easily. It felt odd, considering they didn't have to abduct anyone and read their memories.
These monks were able to predict their arrival, they knew Nux was hiding in another Timeline, they also knew he was an Anomaly, and yet they still didn't do anything and just gave in.
Riona didn't like the sound of it.
And Nux wasn't any different.
He was quite paranoid as well. He nodded at his women and prepared to leave.
"If something happens, I will kill myself."
He chuckled as he said those words. The women chuckled as well, and then, Nux disappeared, arriving right in front of the Temple.

The Temple was ancient, carved from shimmering stone that shifted colors with the passing wind—sometimes gold, sometimes silver, like time itself couldn't decide. Massive pillars twisted upward, spiraling like the hands of a clock frozen mid-motion.
An enormous door stood at the center, etched with countless symbols that even Nux, with all the knowledge he had in his head, couldn't recognize.

He even felt the air around him change the moment he entered the Temple's area of influence. His eyes couldn't move away from that giant door, and in the end, as if tempted by some unknown force, he walked in with a dull look on his face, almost as if he were hypnotized.
And the moment he entered,
Swhoosh
His powers were stripped away.

chapters.title: Chapter 1994 [Trial One: River of Eternity]
paragraphs: Nux stared at the giant gates in front of him with a lost look on his face, then, as if an unknown force was calling him in, he started walking. The action felt almost unconscious. Nux only returned to his senses when his hand was just about to touch the gates.
He wanted to stop and understand what had just happened, but it was already too late.
His hand had pushed through the gates. The giant gates opened with unintended ease, almost as if they were waiting for another participant.
The moment the doors opened, Nux's body was sucked in.
It was an odd feeling. Nux tried to resist it, but once again, he couldn't.
For the first time in a long while, things felt like they were out of his control—an experience that scared him, but it was also something that made him look forward to this place even more.

A few seconds later, Nux found himself inside a white space. The place had no walls; it stretched endlessly with a white floor and a similar roof above him. Wherever he looked, he could only see endless white—nothing else.
It wasn't just the space around him, even his own body was similar. He stared at his hands and realized his entire body had turned white as if someone had painted him with white paint.
No, that was not it.
This...
This wasn't his body.
Nux finally realized it.

His powers were gone. Even his physical strength wasn't the same as before. Not just that, he couldn't even connect to his Universe or his wives. He even tried returning to his Universe and realized he couldn't do it. Now that he was inside, he was on his own.
While the mass and body structure of this body felt similar to his own, Nux knew it wasn't his own body.
He...
He seemed to have been trapped inside a body of a mannequin that was modeled after his own body.
'What the...'
He wondered. He waved his hand, wanting to summon a mirror to look at what his face looked like, but he couldn't.
His powers didn't work.
Law of Space, or the storage ring, or any other power for that matter—no matter what he did, nothing worked.

His powers were gone. Even his physical strength wasn't the same as before. Not just that, he couldn't even connect to his Universe or his wives. He even tried returning to his Universe and realized he couldn't do it. Now that he was inside, he was on his own.
He had turned into a Mortal again, just that because of his body structure, he was an absurdly strong mortal who should be able to defeat at least 10 other mortals without any issues.
'So it did work on me.'
Nux seemed impressed.
When he read that some of the Trials stripped away the Trial Takers' powers, he wondered if it would work on him considering who he was. But now...
'I underestimated this place.'
Nux admitted.
Then, as he stretched and got somewhat used to his new body, he started walking forward. He didn't know where he was going or what he was supposed to do, he just felt like walking, so he did.
As if sensing that he was prepared, a screen appeared in front of Nux.
[Trial One: River of Eternity]
'Well, this brings back memories.'
Nux chuckled as he saw a screen hovering in front of him. The screen was in no way similar to his system. It was a simple translucent gold screen with a small message.

As the screen appeared, Nux's surroundings started to change. The white floor beneath him began to form dust as it started its transformation. Within a few seconds, Nux was standing on what seemed like a beach.
He looked ahead and saw a large ocean with strong waves ahead of him.
At the very end of the ocean, there seemed to be an island, and as Nux's eyes fell on the island, another screen appeared in front of him.
[Cross the River of Eternity and reach the other end.]
Yes, that was it.
That was the first trial.
And Nux, who saw this, stared at the screen in front of him as his mouth twitched.
'Who in their right mind calls this a river!?'
He cursed.
He recalled the records of Trials he had read, and some of the Trials were similar to this. Even Vashti had passed through such a trial, and according to her reports,
The water in the River of Eternity isn't normal water, but a physical manifestation of time itself.

Of course, Nux had no clue what that meant. Neither did Vashti bother explaining it. It was similar to how one's comprehension couldn't be taught to someone. While the records did contain the information regarding the Trials, they didn't mention a way to clear those trials—else everyone would have done that already.
Nux was indeed on his own.
'Meh, no point thinking about it.'
Nux shrugged.
Since he was told to cross the river, that is what he was going to do.
He stepped into the water. First, it was his right leg that stepped in, then it was his left.
Then it finally happened.

The right side of his body shrivelled up. His skin got loose, muscles weakened, and wrinkles started appearing all over his body. Yes, the right side of his body had aged up—so much that his knee couldn't even support his body.
This, however, wasn't the only problem he was facing.
Rather, this might be the easier part.

While the right part of his body had aged, the left part had regressed. His arms and legs were now comparable to that of a toddler's. He didn't even dare to look at what his face currently looked like, and honestly, that was the least of his worries.
The biggest problem was his inability to walk.
With his body completely disproportionate, he fell into the river, with absolutely no control over his body.
'What is this place...?'

He wondered as he stayed on the water. The only thing he was relieved about was that his body was still on the ground, so the water current didn't take him away. This, however, didn't solve any of his problems.
His body still seemed like it was changing, with the right side getting older and older, and the left getting younger.
He had to do something, or else he would perish—and he would in an extremely bizarre manner, with the right side dying of old age, while the left disintegrated out of existence.
'I am royally fucked, aren't I?'

chapters.title: Chapter 1995 Easy Peazy!
paragraphs: 'I am royally fucked, aren't I?'
Nux cried.
Yes, he literally cried.
Because one side of his body had aged and the other had regressed, right now, he was a strange combination of a child and an old man, and in both cases, he had next to no control over his body.
His mind, that had sensed the threat, started working, his heart started beating faster, and his eyes...
They teared up.
Soon, however, he noticed something.
The speed of his death had... slowed down.
While the left side of his body was getting younger and younger, the right side... it had slowed down a little. It was still getting older, just at a comparatively slower pace.
He frowned.
Unable to understand why this was happening.
'Is getting older more difficult than getting younger?'
He wondered.
Soon, however, he threw that idea out of his head.
It was something else, something he hadn't noticed till now. He looked around and realized something.
As he had fallen on the ground, no water had gone behind him.
The sand behind him was dry.
Almost as if...
His body was absorbing the water.
Right now, Nux was on his knees, his body was tilted since his body was strongly disproportionate, so he was also forced to use his elbows to support himself.
He looked down at the water beneath him and finally realized it.
It was not an as if situation, his body was absorbing the water.

As his right, grown arm was on the ground, it had started absorbing some of the water, similar to how his legs had been absorbing the water all this while. And since his right arm was absorbing the water, his right leg didn't get much water to absorb.
Now, instead of his right leg, the right water was being absorbed by his right elbow and forearm.
His right arm, however, wasn't just absorbing the right water; his palm, which had supported itself in front of his left arm and leg, was absorbing some of the left water.
Nux's mind worked, and he came up with a theory.

If the right water was making him older and the left water was making him younger, then the right part of his body, which was absorbing some of both left and right water, must have slowed down the aging process.
It wasn't just that—the left part of his body, which was now receiving less left water, must have slowed down as well, just not as significantly as the right part.
And this was exactly what was happening with Nux.
'This might work.'
Suddenly, another idea popped into Nux's head as he nodded.
If he didn't do anything, he would die, and since there was no time to test his theory, he decided to act on whatever he had.
The control he had over the left side of his body was extremely limited, and while moving his right side was still difficult, he could move it.
And that is what he did.

He moved the right part of his body towards the left water as he rotated his body. It was difficult, his muscles had next to no power, he was pretty much dragging his body, and his movement was extremely slow.
"Haaah... Haaahh... Haaahh..."
Within a few seconds, he was already out of breath. Yes, that was how old his body had gotten.
However, not everything was in vain.
As more and more of his right body got to the left water, the amount of right and left water in the right side of his body became equal.
His right body wasn't aging anymore.
It was working.
Just that...
Since his left body was comparatively smaller, the amount of right water it could absorb was limited, and most of the water it was absorbing was left.
Yes, his right side was still regressing.
He was already at the level of a newborn and didn't have quite a lot of time left.
"Haaaahh!!"
So Nux decided to force himself and gave his body one last push.
Crack
And his bone cracked.
"Gaah!! Fuck!"
He cursed as he fell down, his right arm trembling in pain.
Yes, his body was no longer strong enough to endure all the agonizing pain like he was trained to— even a little bone crack was more than enough to make him whimper.
The good part, however, was that he succeeded.
The right part of his body was now absorbing left water, and the left part of the body was absorbing the right water.
His aging had reversed.
His left body was now aging, and the right one started regressing.
What's even better was that even his wound had regressed and returned to normal.
"Haaaaahh... haahh... haaaahh..."
He took deep breaths of relief as he lay on the ground, letting his body return to its normal state.
No.
That wasn't the place.
As his left body grew and reached the level of a 10-year-old child, he finally moved.
His right body was not as old as before, so he had somewhat gotten his control back. The aim was now to continue crossing the river.
And while he was currently facing the opposite direction, it didn't matter.
Nux started crawling backwards.
His body continued to become more and more proportionate as both sides of his body got better and better. His speed also increased as the river was now 20 cm deep.
Nux continued to move. Soon, he was forced to swim as the water became deeper and deeper. A few more seconds later, his body had returned to normal.
A feeling he relished quite a lot.
He finally realized what a blessing a normal body was.
This feeling, however, didn't last for long.
The situation had reversed, his left body had now started aging while the right had started regressing.

Not that he was surprised—Nux had expected this. Rather, he was prepared for this. He continued to swim backwards as fast as he could, allowing his body to age differently. Then, the moment the right part of his body reached around the size of a 15-year-old, he turned around and reversed the flow again.
Yes, he finally found the way out.
'Hmph! Easy Peazy!' He grinned.
He grinned

chapters.title: Chapter 1996 Fuck
paragraphs: 'Hmph! Easy Peazy!'
Nux grinned.
He had finally done it.
Clearing the Trial that so many failed to, even some people from the Supreme Worlds had failed before.
'I guess the Supreme Worlds aren't as special as they think they are, huh...'
Nux sighed like a disappointed Asian father.
'To think they couldn't clear the first trial, it wasn't even that difficult. I cleared it without many difficulties.'
He muttered as he rotated his body again, once again reversing the flow of time inside his body as he continued to swim, getting closer and closer to the end.
Yes, it was indeed very easy.
Nux nodded to himself, confident.
A mistake.
Nux had raised a flag, a shameful feat considering that he, out of all people, knew how dangerous flags were.
But honestly, he couldn't be blamed either.
The poor man had knowledge of multiple worlds in his head, one couldn't find faults with him for forgetting his roots and culture for a moment.
Of course, his blunder wouldn't go unpunished.
The River, as if knowing exactly what he was thinking, made a move.
Nux's expression changed as he sensed something.
Right now, the left side of his body had become younger, so much that he was about to rotate any second now, but suddenly, his attention was attracted by something else.
A tremor.
The water he was swimming in suddenly trembled.
It wasn't a simple ripple, but a deep, unnatural shudder, like the ocean itself had tensed. Nux's frown deepened.
This... wasn't normal.
He momentarily paused and looked around. For the first few mini seconds, he saw nothing,
But then...
On the horizon, he saw it—a dark line.
'Fuck...'
He cursed.
The line grew taller, wider, rushing toward him with terrifying speed.
Yes, it was a wave, and it was huge. It was like a wall, a mountain of water, and the closer it got, the more Nux realized how fucked he actually was.
Gulp
He gulped, finally realizing his mistake.
He tried to move and outrun the wave, but...
This task was difficult even when his body was at its best. After all, in this place, he was only a mortal.
And adding his disproportionate body into the factor, it was pretty much impossible to get away.
'Fuck it!'
Nux cursed and tried anyway.
And just as he expected, he failed.

He couldn't even move a meter away before the giant wave was right above him. He looked back, staring at the wave. This time, it looked much larger than before. He couldn't even see the end of it as he looked up.
And finally, the wave engulfed, then it crashed down.
The water slammed down on his helpless body. He tried moving, thrashing, or resisting, but his disproportionate body made it impossible to do anything.
As his body twisted and turned inside the river, now, for some reason, it wasn't his right and left body that was being affected, it was his upper and lower body.
Yes, his upper body was now growing older, while his lower body had started becoming younger.
What's worse?
His body had still not stopped absorbing the water, so now the right-left water was entering his body from every possible side, and it had made a mess out of his body even further.
As his body twisted and turned inside the river, now, for some reason, it wasn't his right and left body that was being affected, it was his upper and lower body.
Yes, his upper body was now growing older, while his lower body had started becoming younger.

And just when he got used to it, things reversed. Now, his lower body grew, while the upper became younger. Then once again, the changes started happening in the right and left sides of his body, before it returned to upper and lower again.
The cycle continued. His body became messier and messier. Almost every single part of his body was stuck in a different age and the worst part?
The water was still pushing him down.
It was over.
He was swallowed. Some of his body parts were close to disintegrating out of existence, some were about to die of old age.
The only reason he was even alive till now was that every time a part of his body was about to perish, fortunately, the waves turned him away and the aging reversed, helping him survive.

Yes, Nux was that helpless. He could only rely on his luck, and even that was running thin now since his body was constantly being 'divided' into more and more 'parts', with each part aging differently.
Even luck couldn't help him with this. No matter what position his body was in, it didn't matter, since one part of his body would age or disintegrate.
In the end, Nux closed his eyes and gave up.
His mind had already started thinking about ways to clear the trial once everything reset.

Yes, according to the records he read, one never dies during these trials. The trials are usually reset, giving the Trial Taker a chance to take the trial again, just that most of the time, it creates a situation so helpless that the Trial Taker doesn't even bother trying it again.
Just like right now, Nux's mind raced to its limit, yet he failed to come up with a way. How was he even supposed to do anything when he was no different than a mortal?
No matter how he thought about it, clearing the trial seemed... impossible.
Slowly, Nux's body was pushed back to the edge, from where he had begun. Once he returned to the sand, his body, which was divided into parts, started returning to its normal state.
The sand seemed to have some sort of healing power in it.
Within 5 minutes, Nux returned to his peak condition and finally stood up. Once again, he stared at the river-cum-ocean in front of him and sighed.
Even now, he still couldn't come up with a way to clear the trial.
Soon, however, his expression changed as he noticed something.
His body...
There seemed to be a different form of energy flowing through his body.
He tried to move this energy, and suddenly, water came out of his palm, and his palm started aging up.
He somehow controlled the water as it returned to his body, and once again, his arm returned to normal.
Nux's expression changed.
He...
He now seemed to have the power of water that his body had absorbed all this while.

No matter what position his body was in, it didn't matter, since one part of his body would age or disintegrate.
In the end, Nux closed his eyes and gave up.
His mind had already started thinking about ways to clear the trial once everything reset.
Yes, according to the records he read, one never dies during these trials.

The trials are usually reset, giving the Trial Taker a chance to take the trial again, just that most of the time, it creates a situation so helpless that the Trial Taker doesn't even bother trying it again.
Just like right now, Nux's mind raced to its limit, yet he failed to come up with a way.
How was he even supposed to do anything when he was no different than a mortal?
No matter how he thought about it, clearing the trial seemed... impossible.
Slowly, Nux's body was pushed back to the edge, from where he had begun.
Once he returned to the sand, his body, which was divided into parts, started returning to its normal state.
The sand seemed to have some sort of healing power in it.
Within 5 minutes, Nux returned to his peak condition and finally stood up.
Once again, he stared at the river-cum-ocean in front of him and sighed.
Even now, he still couldn't come up with a way to clear the trial.
Soon, however, his expression changed as he noticed something.
His body...
There seemed to be a different form of energy flowing through his body.
He tried to move this energy, and suddenly, water came out of his palm, and his palm started aging up.
He somehow controlled the water as it returned to his body, and once again, his arm returned to normal.
Nux's expression changed.
He...
He now seemed to have the power of water that his body had absorbed all this while.

chapters.title: Chapter 1997 The Reward.
paragraphs: "Hmmmmmmm."
Nux tilted his head as he stared at his palm that constantly released water and absorbed it again, all while it got aged, returned to normal, then regressed and returned to normal again.
Yes, Nux's control over the water inside his body seemed to have increased.

He finally understood how things worked. If he moved the water inside his body clockwise before releasing it, it would age his hands. If he did the opposite and moved it counterclockwise, it would regress his hands.
One thing to note, however, was that every time he moved the water in and out of his body, some of it dropped on the sand and was absorbed, never to return.
So the conversion wasn't absolute.
Every time he used his new 'power', he lost some of it, and once he ran out...
He would lose his newly gained power.
"It makes sense now."
Nux nodded inwardly.

He remembered how Vashti, in her report, mentioned that the Temple rewards the Trial Taker and tempts him to go away after every single attempt. Just that once the Trial Taker accepts the temptation and returns, the Temple never rewards him again, no matter how many times he returns or how many Trials they clear.
"So this is my 'reward', huh..."
Nux muttered as he once again regressed his hands.
"The power of time over my own body.
If I return now..."
He could have this power for himself.
Just as he thought about it, a Gate formed behind him, showing him the way out.
Nux also noticed that more and more water continued to leak out of his palm—
His powers were going away.
If he didn't move out now, he would lose quite a big chunk of his power. Yes, it was yet another way the Temple sent the Trial Taker away. It was almost as if it wanted people to leave.
Of course, Nux didn't budge.
He just turned toward the River of Eternity and started thinking. Now that he had this power, things felt easier.

He simply needed to release as much water as his body absorbed to keep the balance. It was all about energy control—something he was sort of a master at. After all, he was used to controlling multiple energies in his body at once.

With newfound confidence, he walked toward the river again. He stepped in. Once again, the water entered his right leg and started aging it. At the same time, he started moving the water in his own body counterclockwise and released the water through his leg, trying to regress it.

The two forces canceled each other out, and just as Nux expected, his leg was perfectly fine. Nux walked further. Now, his left leg was in as well and had started regressing. He moved the water in his body clockwise and released it through his left foot, stabilizing the effect.
With the situation now under his complete control, he walked forward. The water had no effect on his body. Soon, he was already 100 cm deep into the water, so he started swimming.

Again, his body wasn't affected. Even when the time flow reversed and the right water started regressing his body instead of aging it, he simply changed the flow of energy inside his own body and balanced it.
It was absolutely effortless.
Nux continued to swim and once again, he saw a dark line at the horizon as the water started trembling.
Yes, the wave was here again.
'Heh.'
He grinned.
It was something he was looking forward to. He wanted to know how effective his plan was.

Soon, the wave came, and Nux allowed it to engulf him. His body twisted and rotated as the water pushed it in different directions. Once again, his body started dividing into different 'parts', with each part aging differently.
Nux expected this, and to counter it, he moved the water inside his own body, releasing it from every single part that was formed.

Now, he needed to constantly change the water flow in his own body to take care of every single 'part' of his body at the same time, all while the water continued to change its property of regressing or aging him, forcing him to change the flow as well.

It was something almost every being would lose their mind in. After all, his mind had to take care of hundreds of different parts in his body and stabilize them, all while trying to find his way back to the surface.
His brain was forced to multitask on hundreds of different fronts, but...
To Nux, it didn't really matter.
Honestly, he had already ingrained the water flow into his mind to the point his body was now doing it on its own.
Yes, Zenith Flow was already activated.

He had activated it and trained his body while he was testing his ability at the shore. After doing it multiple times, training his body to manipulate a single 'energy' was almost as easy as breathing for him.
He only needed to find a way back to the surface, which he did after a few minutes.
Yes, the wave had disappeared, the water was stabilized, and finally, the 'end' was near.
This time, however, Nux remembered his culture. He wasn't planning on raising any flags. He simply nodded to himself and continued to swim, still wary of anything that might happen.
And just as he expected, something did happen.
The water inside his body 'ran out', meaning that he no longer had the power to manipulate time inside his body. The river water could now once again alter his body as it pleased.
Of course, Nux didn't give up. Since the wave was gone, his body was now only divided into two parts—left and right—just like how it was in the beginning.
So his counter was the same. He swam, and once the disproportion in his body grew, he rotated his body and swam backwards.
This, however, didn't make him any happier.
After all,
He could already see another dark line on the horizon.
The second wave was here.

chapters.title: Chapter 1998 Time here is frozen.
paragraphs: "Uggghhh..."
Nux groaned as he once again returned to the surface. The sand reversed whatever 'damage' had happened to him as he stood up again, his eyes staring at the ocean in front of him.
The moment his 'powers' disappeared, the second wave that appeared crushed him almost instantly. He tried resisting, but he was helpless.
In the end, his body was pushed back to the shore.
Nux, however, did notice one good thing.
Since he was inside the water longer than before, the amount of water he had absorbed was higher than before. It also meant the power he now had was stronger.
Just as he thought about it, a Gate appeared behind him.

The Temple was tempting him to go away yet again, this time with the power stronger than before. Of course, Nux didn't care. His mind was still thinking of a way to clear the trial and... he did have a way.
So without further ado, Nux walked forward, entering the water without wasting more time.

Once again, he swam as he controlled the water inside his body. Since his powers had gotten stronger, his control had gotten smoother as well. Not that it mattered to him — his control was already next to perfect. The only good thing that came out of it was that he now didn't need to use as much 'power' as he did before to deal with the river's aging or regressing, meaning his powers would last even longer, probably until he crossed the river and reached the end.
As he thought about it, the first wave came.
Once again, Nux allowed it to engulf him. His body was divided into parts, and once again, Nux dealt with it the same way he did before.
He returned to the surface, and this time, since he had more water in his body and better control, his powers were still there.
So he continued to swim.
The second wave came, but Nux survived. He returned to the surface and saw the third wave approaching, and he survived that as well.
Now, however, the water ran out again.
With his powers gone, the fourth wave drowned him.
He returned to the shore, and the sand healed his body again. He realized that his body had now absorbed even more water. Yes, his power grew even stronger.
The Gate appeared again, telling him to leave.
But now, there was no reason to.
Nux had found a way out.
This place took his powers, but at the same time, it was also giving him a new set of powers — powers he could strengthen through his own efforts.
It was a trial fair for all, a trial where everyone had the same, equal start.
It was quite idealistic, but to Nux, it was fun.
Now that he had found a way to increase his powers, that was what he was going to do.
The system seemed clear now — the more time he spent in the water, the more powerful he became. The more powerful he becomes, the closer he gets to the end.
All he needed to do was to continue trying, again and again, until he finally reached the end and cleared the trial.
It was a simple brute-force method, something that Nux didn't hate.
As he stretched his body, Nux entered the water again.
The first wave, just like always, was no problem.
The same was true for the second, third, fourth, and fifth. On the sixth wave, however, the water ran out, and Nux was pushed back to the shore, stronger than before.

He grinned and jumped into the water again, clearing all six waves as he moved forward. The closer he got to the end, the stronger the waves and the more frequent they got, dividing Nux's body into thousands of 'parts,' with each part aging differently and needing a different flow of energy to be stabilized.
It was something that would overwhelm anyone's mind, but to Nux, this didn't seem like a problem. His body was acting on its own — he just needed to swim and get close to the end.
The eighth wave came, then the ninth, the tenth, and once again, at the eleventh wave, Nux failed and returned to the shore again.
The Gate appeared, telling him to leave, but he didn't.
The now-stronger Nux returned to the water. This time, he cleared fourteen waves before failing.
On the next run, he managed to clear sixteen waves.
Then seventeen.
Eighteen, nineteen, twenty...
All the way to ninety-nine and...
In the most recent run, he cleared the hundredth wave.

Yes, it took about two hundred tries. The waves divided his body into a million parts; Nux had to move energy through almost all the pores inside his body to survive, and that was exactly what he did.
And now...
The end was finally in front of him now, barely three meters away.
Nux also didn't see any more waves forming to stop him, so he decided to use this chance to increase his speed and race toward the shore.
And he succeeded. His hand was now 1 cm away from the shore. Even if a wave was generated now, it wouldn't be able to stop him.
The trial was over. It should be over.
But then suddenly...
Nux's finger, which was about a centimetre away from the shore, froze.
It couldn't move.
Nux frowned. He tried using force, but no matter what he did, his finger didn't budge. Then finally, he noticed something.
The last 1 cm that he had to cross...
The water in this region was... not moving.
Its ripples were frozen, just like his finger — almost as if...
'Time here is frozen.'
And since time was frozen... movement here was impossible.
'How the fuck...'
Nux cursed again, his mind thinking of ways to cross the frozen zone, but nothing came to his mind.
To make things worse, another wave was formed and engulfed him. This time, however, it couldn't push him down since his finger was stuck in the frozen zone.
Of course, Nux still had to use his 'energy' to avoid perishing, and soon, his energy ran out.

As it did, another wave appeared and engulfed his body again. This time, for some reason, his finger was released from the frozen zone, and his body, once again, returned to the shore, where it all had begun.
Once again, he had failed to clear the trial.

chapters.title: Chapter 1999 A New Law.
paragraphs: Nux sighed as he stared at the Gate in front of him.

He had failed the Trial, and the Gate had appeared in front of him again. Since he had reached the very end of the river, the amount of 'water' his body had absorbed increased significantly, raising his power to an absurd degree.
If he left in this state, the Law he would receive would be quite strong.
He, however, had to make a quick decision here.
While his body had absorbed quite a lot of water, the rate at which it was releasing the water had also increased quite a bit. Nux was losing his newly gained power much quicker than before.
What's worse?
This loss of power wasn't stopping.

Even when Nux re-entered the River, reached the end of the River, failed again, and returned to the shore, the water in his body didn't get refilled; it stayed the same as it was when he re-entered the river and...
It was still falling rapidly.
It was almost as if the Temple was telling him to hurry up and leave or...
Abandon whatever progress he had made and lose all his powers.
Nux stared at his palm, observing the water flowing out as he started thinking.
This Trial...
It was difficult.
Too difficult, in fact.

The Temple of Time was created to help beings form Laws related to Time. So technically, most beings who enter these Trials should only be Semi Saint or Saint Level Cultivators, cultivators without a Law.

This Trial, however... it was simply impossible for a Saint to clear it. Controlling the flow of 'water' inside his body and countering the aging and regressing of a million different parts of his body, all while trying to swim back to the surface—
No Saint Level Cultivator would be able to do it.
Heck, a Divine, Primordial, or even a Transcendent shouldn't be able to do it. Only Eternal Level beings, who have almost perfect control over their energy, would be able to reach as far as he did.
Why is a Trial designed for a Saint so difficult?
Something didn't feel right.
Yes, Nux did remember that the Trial was modified according to the Trial Taker's abilities, so it was likely that the difficulty was adjusted for him, but...
Weren't all his powers and abilities taken away anyway?
Here, he was no different than a mortal with a slightly stronger body. His presence shouldn't alter the Trial's degree to this extent.
Something was wrong.
No, Nux was missing something.
He closed his eyes and started thinking. His body continued to release all the water, losing all the power he had gained, but Nux didn't care.
His instincts told him that he needed to look at the Trial from a different perspective.
The Temple of Time was created to help beings form Laws related to Time...
No, that was not what the documents Tenzin had given him said.
The Temple of Time, it didn't help one form Laws related to Time; it helped one understand Time.
He was here to comprehend the Concept of Time.
The river in front of him and the water inside him, it gave him power over time. It taught him how to use this power, how to manipulate time inside his body to resist the change outside.
This, however, was not the main goal.
After all, Nux still didn't understand the Concept of Time; he just had the Power over it. The power he had depended on the amount of water he had absorbed.
It was never his power that came from his understanding.
It was a distraction.
Just like the Gate.

The Trial was never about using the power gained to cross the river. This was also the reason the Temple made it impossible to clear the Trial that way. No one was supposed to reach the very end using the power given by the Trial; they should have drowned under the waves and returned to shore.
Only a monster like Nux could possibly use a borrowed power and get this far.
But even he couldn't clear the Trial using the wrong method.
Nux realized it.
The Power given to him was merely a reference—something for him to lean on to understand Time itself, or in this case, understand the Flow of Time itself.
Nux sat down and started recalling everything he had done—how he controlled the 'water' inside his body to resist the 'water currents' outside.
As he continued to do that, his mind recalled the words Vashti had used in her report:
The water in the River of Eternity is a physical manifestation of Time itself.
If the water was time, the water currents were the Flow of Time. What Nux was doing all this while was going against the violent Flow of Time while using the energy inside his own body.
Not a very smart decision.
After all, the energy inside his body was limited. So was the 'space'; he couldn't move the energy around as he desired.
He needed to do something different.
He needed to clear the Trial the way it was meant to be cleared.
He needed to understand the Flow of Time and learn how to change it through his will.

With that thought in his mind, Nux once again started replaying everything that happened when he tried to cross the river. He observed how the Flow of Time changed his body, he observed when it was violent and when it was comparatively calm, he also analyzed how the Power of Time he had absorbed worked.
Nux sat there for weeks, or maybe it was months, years, or decades—he didn't know. The Flow of Time in this place was different.
It couldn't be clearly sensed, neither did he try to.
Only when he felt that he was ready did he finally open his eyes and stare at the River of Eternity in front of him.
Then, he stood up, stepped forward, and suddenly, he disappeared and appeared right in front of the river.
No, he didn't teleport—he didn't have that ability here.
What he did have here, however, was the ability to alter the Flow of Time around him.
Yes, using the river as a reference, the monster had comprehended a way to manipulate the Flow of Time.
He had formed a new Law.
